Charred vehicles line empty roads littered with the debris of destroyed buildings, while the thud of artillery fire gives way to the sharp, high-pitched hum of an attack drone.

This is today's reality in the eastern Ukrainian town of Druzhkivka, where a remnant of civilians live alongside troops fighting Russian forces who are now only 15 km (nine miles) away and steadily edging closer.

Widespread ruin of this nature is mirrored along the entire 1,200-km (746-mile) front line across the east and south. As Russian forces push ahead, apartment blocks, local markets and shops are flattened, rendering whole communities virtually uninhabitable.

open image in gallery A destroyed apartment building, amid Russia's attack on Ukraine, in the frontline town of Druzhkivka in Donetsk region, Ukraine August 25, 2026 ( Reuters )

"I can't sleep," said Iryna ​Litovchenko, ⁠one of a handful of civilians who have stayed. "Some guys took us in - strangers," added the 56-year-old, walking through broken glass and debris beside badly damaged buildings.

"My ⁠home is gone, as if it never existed. There were so many good things, ​so ⁠much of everything. In one fell ‌swoop – boom — it's as if nothing's left."

Druzhkivka lies on the road linking strategic towns and cities known as the "fortress belt", a string of urban settlements that Russia is desperate ‌to breach as it tries to seize the whole ‌of Ukraine's eastern Donbas region.

Map of Druzhkivka:

That remains one of Russian President Vladimir Putin's primary objectives in the war, but well over four years after he launched a full-scale invasion, his forces are struggling to break through Ukraine's ⁠defences.

open image in gallery A destroyed apartment building, amid Russia's attack on Ukraine, in the frontline town of Druzhkivka in Donetsk region, Ukraine August 25, 2026. REUTERS/Stringer TPX IMAGES OF THE DAY/File Photo ( Reuters )

Litovchenko does not flinch at the loud blast from a nearby howitzer. But when she hears the soft buzz of a drone above, she stops before taking shelter under the branches of a tree.

Thousands of Russian and Ukrainian unmanned aerial vehicles, most steered remotely by pilots, fill the skies close to the front, hunting their prey with deadly efficiency.

In Druzhkivka, and all along the fortress belt, many roads are ‌covered with netting to protect anyone travelling on them from drones. An unmanned ​ground vehicle, used to supply frontline Ukrainian positions and evacuate wounded soldiers, whizzes ‌towards its next mission.

open image in gallery A Ukrainian serviceman fires to shoot down a Russian drone, amid Russia's attack on Ukraine, in the frontline town of Druzhkivka in Donetsk region, Ukraine August 26, 2026 ( Reuters )

Zoya, a 63-year-old ⁠selling basic food items outside a charred market stall, does not want to ⁠leave her home town, despite the dangers.

"I know a bomb could come flying in and I'll die. I understand ‌that perfectly well."

"It's heartbreaking," ​she added, pointing to the destruction around her. "It ‌makes me want to cry. I ​was born here, I grew up here. I just don't know. Our city is gone."

News.title: Manchester United’s attack may be their best form of defence this season
News.content:
Is attack going to be Manchester United’s best form of defence this season, then?

There was plenty to like going forward, particularly once United had nudged their way in front after their second lucky break of what had hitherto looked like being a tricky afternoon.

Give this team a little space and they have the attacking players to inflict some serious damage, none more so than Bruno Fernandes who, just five days after collecting the PFA Players’ Player of the Year award, scored a hat-trick amidst another inspired performance.

Ipswich Town will testify to that after a sobering second half when it felt like United were going to score with every raid forward and, for a time, even threaten to equal the nine goals they scored against the promoted side at this ground 31 years ago.

In the returning Marcus Rashford, whom manager Michael Carrick likened to a “new signing”, Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo and, of course, Fernandes, United have an intriguing blend of attacking players. Throw in Kobbie Mainoo who, on another day, would have stolen the headlines with an imperious display in central midfield, and one thing United are not lacking for is creativity.

News.title: Robinson’s Victorian-style bowling figures secure series victory over Pakistan
News.content:
The only missing aspect was a five-fer which would have brought a 100th Test wicket. Even so, his career average is now 19.53, the best for England since Frank Tyson of those with 50 or more wickets.

Mr Nude Nuts, as Matthew Hayden called him, could be devastating against Australia and, like Root the captain, deserves to be judged on what happens in his second incarnation rather than what went before.

Robinson’s pace has lingered around the 79mph mark and inevitably that throws up Rob Key’s assertion you cannot succeed in Test cricket bowling in the 70s with the keeper standing up. Key was referring to county bowlers pitching it up and relying on the Dukes ball to do the rest.

It was thrown in his face in Australia but Michael Neser and Scott Boland are not county trundlers: they extract more energy off the pitch than that.

Robinson is also no dobber. His high release point combined with a mastery of length means he is always threatening the top of off stump. He also knows which way the ball is going to nip, giving no clues to the batsmen due to his sleight of hand skills.

With Jamie Smith improving under the tutelage of Sarah Taylor, he can operate with the keeper standing up which pins batsmen in the crease, bringing all modes of dismissals into play. Robinson was as effective with the new ball as the old: his two seven-over spells were two for 13 and two for 11.

How snarling Robinson adds edge and precision

At 32, he has become a combination of Stuart Broad and James Anderson, although down on their pace with the height and bounce of the former, and tricks of the latter. He can move the new ball further either way than Anderson or Broad but the question is whether he has their durability and sheer competitiveness.

He has not been tested this summer by pitches or opponents. He has not bowled more than 18 overs in an innings and was injured when England played on the best batting pitch at the Oval. He was not trusted at Trent Bridge because the old management had burned their fingers before. That decision may well have cost the coach his job.

Like Broad and Anderson he has a snarl too, sending Abdullah Shafique on his way with a word or two. There was no need for that but maybe it was just a carried away reaction to bowling an absolute beauty that angled in, seamed away and hit the top of off.

News.title: Chelsea are great entertainers but possess clear weakness
News.content:
Xabi Alonso takes charge of his first home Premier League game in charge of Chelsea as they host Brighton at Stamford Bridge. Both sides were in action in two different competitions on Thursday night. Chelsea reached the League Cup third round as they beat Luton 2-0 at Stamford Bridge, with former Brighton man Danny Welbeck scoring on his debut. Brighton meanwhile confirmed their place in the Conference League group stages with a 4-0 aggregate win over Tromso.

Chelsea began their Premier League campaign last Monday in a west London derby against Fulham at Craven Cottage, winning 3-2 in Alonso’s first game as Chelsea boss. Enzo Fernandez was not involved in Chelsea’s squad against Luton on Thursday and has been heavily linked with a move to Manchester City. Alonso was asked about Enzo’s absence on Thursday and did not confirm whether the Argentine would be involved today.

“It was just because of the game today [on Thursday] and we have other players who need minutes,” Alonso said. “[On Wednesday], in the afternoon. It is a decision that I took. Enzo is a good professional. He is training well and I have nothing to say about this. It was just decisions that we have to take thinking about the game that we were playing tonight [Thursday]. We will see for Sunday [today].”

Brighton began their Premier League campaign in emphatic style as they thrashed Aston Villa 4-0 at home seven days ago. Jack Hinshelwood scored twice in that game but will now miss a number of weeks with an ankle injury. They are also without Yankuba Minteh, who has been linked with a move to Liverpool this summer but is unavailable due to injury.

“When the window is closed I demand from him [Minteh] that he is fully committed to this club,” Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler said. “There are dreams and wishes for players, but in the end we always need to figure out what is best for the club.

“We have had an exchange with him. At the moment he is definitely a Brighton player. It is very important to understand his thoughts but also our planning. As a club we try to develop players. The last few years have shown that the whole environment gave him a lot of trust and belief that he is capable of having this progress. It is always a give and take and he has gotten a lot from us.”

Brighton won both Premier League meetings last season, winning 3-1 in this fixture last September. Brighton have won five of their last eight top-flight meetings with Chelsea. Team news from Stamford Bridge to follow shortly.

News.title: Moses Itauma lifted out of ring after losing IBF title bout to Filip Hrgovic
News.content:
Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of the heavyweight clash between Moses Itauma and Filip Hrgovic.

Itauma is on the cusp of becoming a British boxing star, but for now there remain questions. It is not that people doubt his talents, more that he needs to prove them emphatically to the wider boxing world.

At just 21, Itauma has been creating rumblings since 2023. He has 10 straight knockouts. He is undefeated. His last two wins were against Dillian Whyte and Jermaine Franklin, but he is yet to beat a fighter you might regard as a gatekeeper to a title fight.

Hrgovic might normally be seen as that gatekeeper. At 34, the Croatian has plenty of experience in the ring, with 21 fights bringing 20 wins, 15 of them by knockout. His only loss was against Daniel Dubois in 2024, but his wins since then have been against Joe Joyce, David Adeleye and Dave Allen. Not the highest quality, by any means. Hrgovic, then, has something to prove to us too.

However, this is no eliminator, this is for the full IBF world heavyweight championship. A win for Itauma would see him become the second-youngest world heavyweight champion in boxing history.

As Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury circle one another, threatening to never fight at all, Itauma looks set to be Britain’s next heavyweight star. All he has to do is win at the O2 Arena tonight. If he does that, he could then be a fixture at the top of the sport for a decade, perhaps more.

Ringwalks are expected at around 10.30pm for the main event. So if men in dressing gowns is your thing, get ready.

News.title: £380m = zero points: Big-spending Spurs humbled by Newcastle
News.content:
“After the first goal we lost confidence,” said De Zerbi. “The reaction was not good enough, not what I want to see on the pitch. The solution is not to put the head down, but to react.”

To be clear, Spurs were not quite as bad as they had been against Brentford on the opening day. They did create chances here, taking 17 shots and forcing a few terrific saves from Lukas Hornicek, Newcastle’s impressive goalkeeper. But in the key moments they suffered from the same absence of clarity and execution as they did last season. Troublingly, this seemed to affect the new signings as much as it did the longer-serving players.

Of the five new arrivals who featured for Spurs, Tonali was the least effective. The Italian had been vigorously booed by the away fans before kick-off and the travelling Geordies waited with palpable excitement for his first mistake. Much to their delight, it arrived after only three minutes: an underhit pass, in his own half, which directly led to Micky van de Ven picking up a yellow card. Tonali was outshone by new Newcastle midfielder Nico Gonzalez, who excelled only a few days after completing his move from Manchester City.

News.title: Lawrence seizes his opportunity on rain-ruined day at Lord’s
News.content:
On a bleak day for batting, Dan Lawrence seized an opportunity that he must have feared had passed him by.

Lawrence was one of the victims of Bazball excess, shoved up to open in place of Zak Crawley two years ago in a punt that backfired and could have ended his Test career.

It took the sudden retirement of Ben Stokes and an injury to first-choice replacement Sam Curran to open up a position at No 6, Lawrence’s natural home, and it has come at just the right time.

At 29 he is a much more rounded cricketer than the one who debuted in Sri Lanka under Joe Root in 2021 and he showed it here with a hard-fought half-century on a gloomy, dank Saturday when only 25 overs were possible between the frequent drizzly showers, forcing MCC into a 50 per cent ticket refund.

It was a second fifty in three innings since his recall and he will not have faced many tougher conditions than this, with the ball seaming around on a spiteful pitch. With Mohammad Abbas teasing the ball off the surface and the athletic Mohammad Rizwan snaffling everything up to the stumps, this was a real challenge of mind and technique.

Lawrence will never win awards for aesthetic beauty but he chose the right balls to put away in a 66-ball unbeaten 50 that stretched England’s lead to 357 at 177 for seven in their second innings. Lawrence settled any wobbles about Pakistan pulling off a miracle recovery.

News.title: Springboks level Greatest Rivalry series with blood-and-thunder victory over All Blacks
News.content:
South Africa aim to bounce back from losing the first game of the Greatest Rivalry Tour as they take on New Zealand in game two from Cape Town. The All Blacks claimed an impressive 33-16 win in game on in Johannesburg last weekend, outscoring South Africa five tries to one. That victory takes New Zealand above South Africa in the world rankings into top spot.

The Springboks know that a defeat today will mean they cannot win the series. They have not lost two consecutive Tests since November 2022. Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu has been given the nod to start at fly-half but Handre Pollard has pulled out of the matchday squad due to a calf injury.

“There were a handful of positives and negatives last week, but the main thing that let us down was that we created so many chances, but mistakes at crucial times cost us,” South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus said.

“We will put in a lot of work this week to ensure that we are sharp in that regard this weekend because if we had used even some of those chances, the result could have been completely different. That said, we know New Zealand will be charged up after winning last week, and they will want to build on that. But the key for us will be to focus on our game and ensure that we are as effective as possible all around.”

News.title: Iraola fumes at bungling fourth official for costing Liverpool a penalty
News.content:
He did know, though, why Liverpool had needed to drag themselves off the deck again for the second week in a row. Iraola has shown in his opening weeks on Merseyside that he is not someone who seeks excuses.

“A lack of intensity hurt us,” Iraola said with obvious disdain and it was only down to a show of character in the second period that a slovenly first half did not enable Forest to win at Anfield for the third consecutive year, for all that the travelling fans thought it was “happening again!”

Forest, bruised after two defeats in four days to Leeds, looked like an Oliver Glasner side. They were aggressive and well organised, the only failing was that physically they could not see the job through, but the Austrian insisted that will change in due course.

Once Glasner is settled in and he gets his transfer business done – “definitely one, possibly two and probably three,” was his mischievous reply to how the window will unfold – Forest will be a formidable proposition, especially if the first 45 minutes are a barometer.

They had been knocking on the door before Dan Ndoye eventually broke the deadlock, sweeping a left-footed drive past Alisson after Igor Jesus had won a header from a long clearance. It was a simple goal, marginally onside, but it was absolutely deserved.

Sports.title: Fresh misery for dropped Chelsea keeper Robert Sanchez as it’s revealed he was fined for speeding on motorway
Sports.content:
AXED Chelsea goalkeeper Robert Sánchez was caught speeding by a motorway camera, it has been revealed.

The £25million ace, 28, was doing 47mph in a 40mph zone on the M23 in Crawley, Surrey.



Spaniard Sánchez was convicted of speeding and slapped with three licence penalty points.

The player, said to earn £60,000 a week, was also fined £1,520 for the offence last October.



Crawley magistrates’ court dealt with the case in April but it has only just been disclosed in public records, obtained by The Sun.

It came amid concerns over his position as the Blues’ No1 goalie.



He was dropped for yesterday’s match against Brighton after Chelsea signed ­Emiliano Martinez from Aston Villa.

Sánchez arrived at Stamford Bridge from Brighton in 2023.

Sánchez remained Chelsea’s No 1 despite a woeful start against Fulham following two mistakes in Chelsea’s 3-2 win.

No keeper has made more mistakes leading to shots since the start of the 2024/25 season than the Spaniard.



Sánchez’s fine includes a £1,000 financial penalty, a £400 victim surcharge, and £120 court costs.

Sports.title: ‘Best for the team’ – Xabi Alonso tight-lipped over Enzo Fernandez after Chelsea star axed but still no Man City bid
Sports.content:
CHELSEA are prepared for any eventuality after Enzo Fernandez was left out of another squad, with the Blues braced for a double departure.

Fernandez, 25, is pushing for a move to Manchester City before Tuesday’s transfer deadline and has been absent from the last two matchday squads.



Alonso, who made it two Premier League wins from two as Chelsea boss, could not guarantee £100million-rated Pedro Neto, who started and scored against Brighton, would remain at the club.

City are yet to make their first official bid for Fernandez, valued at more than £120m by Chelsea. City are expected to lodge a first bid of around £100m.



Asked if Fernandez had played his final game for the club, Alonso said: “We’ll see.

“We want the best for the team and that’s why we made the decision against Luton and today and anything that happens before Tuesday evening, we need to be aware of what is going to develop.



“We are not sure, we are preparing for all the scenarios but I am sure that whatever happens from Wednesday we will have a good enough squad to compete in all the Premier League games.”

Neto, 26, was in talks over a move to Saudi Pro League side Al-Hilal before Chelsea’s asking price put them off and they turned their attention to Arsenal winger Gabriel Martinelli.

The Portugal international has been involved in all three games under Alonso so far this season and scored his first goal of the season against the Seagulls.

But Alonso declined to say that he would be staying at the club.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

The Spaniard said: “No, in football I don’t guarantee anything, not anyone.

“But I was very happy with Pedro. He did really well, he played with a lot of energy.

“He is going to be very important for the team for the whole season because he has different special qualities.

“He is a threat in one-v-one, he attacks very well in the space, he is strong, he is competitive.



“I am happy that he scored, he was really close to scoring another one. I am very happy with Pedro.”

Romeo Lavia, Joao Pedro and Cole Palmer were also on the scoresheet in Chelsea’s 4-3 win over Brighton.

Sports.title: Bradley Barcola could be £123million mistake for Liverpool… Reds need midfield steel not more flashy wingers
Sports.content:
SOMEONE’S been asleep at the wheel inside Anfield, or the recruitment team led by Richard Hughes is simply blind.

Liverpool’s lack of midfield defensive cover was there for all to see last season.



Glaring holes for the opposition to run through, a lack of bite in the tackle, a naive belief that the attack-minded pair of Dominik Szoboszlai and Alexis Mac Allister could somehow alter their footballing DNA and become dogs of war.

Fast forward to Andoni Iraola’s first home game in charge and it was groundhog day — Nottingham Forest’s quick counter-attacks causing mayhem, Szoboszlai and Mac Allister headless chickens without the ball.



There is joy that sporting director Hughes has finally agreed a transfer fee worth up to £123million with Paris Saint-Germain for Bradley Barcola, who is set to sign on within the next 24 hours on £300,000 a week.

But for all that he is a star attraction, the Frenchman also happens to be a winger.



Rocket science would not be required to work out someone of Barcola’s exciting talent might step up as a marquee successor to departed Mo Salah.

Yet over three months of haggling with the Champions League holders in desperate pursuit of the 23-year-old, a critical weakness was somehow completely ignored.

And the obsession with Barcola could turn into a fatal attraction.

For Oliver Glasner’s side, just like Newcastle did on the opening weekend of the season, ran right through Iraola’s malfunctioning engine room.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Dan Ndoye scored one goal and could have had three, while in the first half Igor Jesus almost had the run of the Liverpool box thanks to precise and pacey passing from behind.

True, Kop ace Florian Wirtz was denied a goal by the tightest of offside margins soon after Ndoye had opened the scoring, having already missed two chances.

But seconds before the break, with chaos all around him, Reds keeper Alisson had to be world class to deny Jesus — and at 2-0 then that would surely have been game over.

The need for someone to get down and dirty, to practice the dark arts and do almost anything to protect the back four is so glaringly clear it is almost laughable.



Yet with the transfer window about to shut nobody with such traits has been brought in.

Liverpool legend Steven Gerrard — no stranger to a biting tackle or a red card in his day — got it in a nutshell.

He stressed of the Iraola side that has now twice had to fire-fight its way to 2-2 draws under him: “They are too nice.

“They’ve got a load of nice technical players but they lack that little bit of nastiness. All over the pitch they have to be more at it, taking yellow cards if they need to. That’s the problem Iraola faces — you need some nastiness, you can’t be so nice.”



At least Victor Munoz, the same age but at around a quarter of Barcola’s price from Osasuna, has a bit about him.

The Spanish World Cup winner’s turn and fierce shot for Liverpool’s second leveller on 82 minutes spoke of a selfless grafter.

But Iraola is overseeing a collection of individuals, not a team, and there is nobody in the middle galvanising them.

Wirtz does look too ‘nice’ and so does the second of last summer’s £100m-plus arrivals, Alexander Isak.



The Swede tapped home the first equaliser but lacks the physicality of a scrapper.

It may well be nice to have Barcola alongside him and Wirtz but if there is no ball-winner, no destroyer, then like the other two so far he could just become another fashion accessory.

Iraola was right to complain that the three minutes of delay as bungling fourth official Tim Robinson fumbled with his subs board with Rio Ngumoha, Ryan Gravenberch and Kostas Tsimikas waiting to go on, gave Forest a window of opportunity.

Yet £50m new boy Liam Delap’s quickly taken throw that ended in a dodgy penalty decision for Neco Williams — with Morgan Gibbs-White converting — once again said it all about lack of cover.

Glasner, hoping to welcome his Crystal Palace old boy Daniel Munoz into the Forest fold, should and could have been celebrating his first win as the new boss.

Iraola is also still without a victory — but crucially still minus a midfield scrapper.

Sports.title: Jude Bellingham praises Jose Mourinho for releasing shackles & giving him ‘freedom’ after red-hot start to Real season
Sports.content:
JUDE BELLINGHAM was Real Madrid’s ‘free lion’ as last season’s crisis club extended their rip-roaring start under Jose Mourinho.

England star Bellingham scored the first and saw another effort put down as an own goal in a mauling of Malaga.



It is three wins in three LaLiga games in the Special One’s second coming as manager at the Bernabeu.

Real — left for dead by Barcelona last term under both Xabi Alonso and Alvaro Arbeloa — have scored 10 goals so far and conceded just two.



Bellingham has been a big part of that and explained why — Mourinho has given him licence to roam.

The Brummie, now fluent in Spanish, said: “I feel more free now. I have more freedom to move, to go up and down the pitch depending on what we need.



“I’m really enjoying my football — and that’s why I’m performing well.”

Kylian Mbappe, scorer of a hat-trick against Real Sociedad on Wednesday, added a third with just half an hour on the clock. And Arda Guler came off the bench to make it four late on.

Bellingham netted first on 19 minutes with a superb solo effort. He out-muscled Angel Recio in the middle of the park before driving at pace into the box.

That left two other challengers trailing before he fired home from a tight angle on the right.

VAR refused to uphold Recio’s cries of foul — and Real were on their way.

Bellingham was unlucky not to claim his side’s second after Mbappe saw a shot parried.

He leapt to head the rebound goalwards but defender Carlos Puga ended up whacking it over the line off keeper Alfonso Herrero.

England reject Trent Alexander-Arnold had been brought back for this one and provided a pinpoint cross from the right four minutes later for Mbappe to convert first time.



It was a 60th LaLiga goal for the France superstar. Only Harry Kane has been scoring more in Europe’s top leagues since Mbappe left Paris Saint-Germain in 2024.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta reveals he’s ‘BEGGING’ Premier League chiefs to make major rule change to overhaul matchday squads
Sports.content:
MIKEL ARTETA has been “begging” Premier League officials to expand matchday squads for the “welfare of the players”.

Rules currently allow managers to name nine substitutes on the bench, an increase from the seven permitted before the Covid-19 pandemic.



But Arteta wants Prem chiefs to increase that so he does not have to leave anyone at home.

The Arsenal boss, whose side go to Aston Villa tonight, has had to leave stars like Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus out of his matchday squad this term and feels it leads to a number of issues — that duo are now both set to leave.



Arteta said: “That’s why I have been begging the Premier League to extend those numbers just for the welfare of the players, which is the most important thing.

“I think every squad needs more than 20 outfield players, ideally, to sustain the level of demand in international games that we have.



“But these are the rules, and within the rules, we have to play.

“We need to be very close to the players to explain those situations in the right way, for everybody to feel important, because they will be.”

The Gunners chief revealed last week that Gabriel Jesus was not part of Arsenal training because of the “numbers in the squad”.

And Arteta does not want to continue having “tough” conversations with players who would rather be with the squad than at home watching on TV.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

He added: “More than anybody, the question has to be to the players.

“What do they want? If they say, ‘no, I prefer to stay at home’, then we have an issue because then they don’t love what they do.

“But I’m sure if you ask players, everybody would like to be part of the squad on matchday.

“Otherwise, you have to tell someone they aren’t even part of the matchday squad. That’s really, really tough. And it doesn’t help anybody.

“It doesn’t help the club, doesn’t help the valuation of the player and doesn’t help them to feel part of it.



“In my opinion, it is a real issue with a really, really simple solution.”

Sports.title: Mario Balotelli slams ‘phones & PlayStations’ for ‘ruining’ football and reveals advice he’d tell his 16-year-old self
Sports.content:
MARIO Balotelli has slammed the impact of mobile phones and video games on football.

The 36-year-old explained that the current crop of young stars coming through have experienced a vastly different upbringing to himself.



Balotelli has noted that he no longer sees young children playing football in the streets in Italy, like when he was a youngster.

He has suggested that modern mobile phone and video game culture is to blame for this shift in entertainment.



The Italian star told The Guardian that the shift now sees young footballers playing less football than previous generations.

Balotelli said: “Computers, phones, and PlayStations have ruined a lot.

“Above all, the parents’ mentality has changed. A seven‑year-old kid today might play football for two hours every three days.

“We had the same structured training sessions, plus three hours of playing at the park every day, which felt like fun but was actually extra training.

“I truly believe talents were born on the street and in the parks.”

He explained that playing against older children helped to raise his game in a way that is less common in the modern age.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

The striker claimed that “it’s very different” because he would learn skills on the streets, rather than just watching videos online.

This upbringing seemed to serve Balotelli well as he went on to score 14 goals in 36 caps for Italy between 2010 and 2018.

Even 20 years after coming through at Lumezzane, Balotelli is continuing to ply his trade professionally for Al-Ittifaq in the UAE First Division.

But it has not been a straight-forward career for the controversial star.

Former Scotland midfielder Scott Brown, 41, even recalled being threatened on the pitch by the striker during a game.



Balotelli’s wild side even threatened to re-emerge after falling out of favour at Genoa last year.

But the Italian has explained that there are lessons he wished he could tell his 16-year-old self.

Balotelli continued: “I’d tell him not to make certain choices and to listen to certain people at specific times.”

Sports.title: Why Arsenal still needed Konsa - despite having so many defenders
Sports.content:
The final hours of the transfer window could see Arsenal bring in an attacker. But before the window shuts, a defensive purchase could take centre stage on Monday night.

Ezri Konsa could be primed for his Arsenal debut at, of all places, the club he has just departed, Aston Villa. Despite not playing any pre-season football in and around his £51m move to north London, Mikel Arteta says Konsa could be ready for a first Gunners outing at Villa Park.

Konsa is not the signing many expected from Arsenal this summer. Arsenal didn't really need a defender, it's one of their strongest areas of the pitch and the attack needed more attention. But they got him anyway.

Aston Villa

Arsenal Monday 31st August 6:30pm Kick off 8:00pm

That does not make Konsa an unnecessary arrival; this could be the buy that helps shore up Arsenal's title defence.

At 28 years old, Konsa is yet another example of the 'win now' stage of Arteta's Arsenal project. They've got the Premier League title but now the target is to create a dynasty.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Gary Neville has questioned the decision for Arsenal to sign another defender in Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa.

As a result, Arsenal have shifted their transfer policy. Around five years ago, it was about signing younger players who can grow into the team. But every year, Arsenal have been signing older and older players on average, as the desire - and the necessity - to win grows more and more.

And in signing two 28-year-olds in Bruno Guimaraes and Konsa, Arsenal are buying older and more experienced players like never before. Experience is the key word - with all four of Arsenal's summer signings to date possessing Premier League football on their CVs.

Yes, the average age of Arsenal signings in the 2024/25 season was at a similar level to the current transfer activity. But Arteta also promoted Ethan Nwaneri and Myles Lewis-Skelly, both 17 at the time, to the first-team squad that year. That would have significantly lowered the average age of Arsenal's first-team regulars.

Konsa is also in the Arsenal team because of a small gap in the squad. William Saliba is currently a long-term absentee, while Jurrien Timber and Ben White have questionable fitness records, so a centre-back who could also cover at right-back was preferable.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ian Wright says he's 'really pleased' with Arsenal signing defender Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa.

However, while Arsenal have some promising young defenders, namely Cristhian Mosquera and Marli Salmon, Mikel Arteta's desire to create a dynasty means no stone can be left unturned.

Mosquera can cover at right-back but gave away a penalty in the Champions League final defeat to Paris Saint-Germain while playing that role. The margins against the very best are so fine.

So Konsa was also brought in for his quality with and without the ball. The England defender is a classic Arteta signing through his duel-winning ability.

The Arsenal manager recognises it as a crucial skill in the game and once said: "When I lose a duel, I am upset" at his players, as seen in the Amazon Prime documentary five years ago.

Image: Ezri Konsa had the best ground duel success rate out of any Premier League defender last season

Well, no Premier League player won more duels on the ground than Konsa, and the England international's lead at the top of this metric is quite significant. He's in a league of his own in this discipline.

But while Konsa is an aggressive player off the ball, he's a calm player on it. Another metric Konsa topped in the Premier League last season is passing accuracy, but a closer look at his numbers recognise a specific skill.

Konsa ranked second for forward passing accuracy, showing his ability to find gaps through the opposition. And given a lot of teams will stand off Arsenal and retreat into a low block, it's a good attribute for the Gunners to have.

But Konsa is also effective when pressed. His 944 passes when under pressure was the sixth-highest out of any Premier League defender last season, while his retention rate - his ability to keep the ball - of 94.8 per cent was the best out of any player in the division.

Image: Ezri Konsa showed a top-level ability to keep the ball and pass it last season

Arteta often speaks about having certain "rules" in the phases when they play out of the back and start attacks. Lose the ball and the team is in trouble and at risk of conceding. Play the right pass early and the gaps emerge for Arsenal's forward players to cause damage.

So while Konsa's signing adds to the defensive solidity that makes Arteta's team what it is, it is also part of an overall plan to improve Arsenal from open play and create spaces earlier in the pitch for Arsenal to benefit from.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player We take a look at the best of Ezri Konsa's during the 2025-2026 Premier League campaign with the England defender being linked with a move to Arsenal.

And with any Arsenal defender, set-piece proficiency has to stand out - and Konsa has a boost in that department too.

Konsa spent one season under the set-piece stewardship of Arsenal dead-ball guru Nicolas Jover while at Brentford in 2018/19, and both have been reunited back in north London.

It is not the only connection the former England international has with the Arsenal squad. Bukayo Saka considers Konsa as part of his 'inner circle' of trusted friends and if Konsa is selected at right-back, it could lead to a promising partnership on the right-hand side.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Bukayo Saka joined us after the Coventry victory to talk fitness, attack, and Ezri Konsa joining Arsenal.

"Ever since I met him at England, we've just got on," Saka told reporters after the win over Coventry on Friday. "Not only because he's a brother to me, but I know the level of player he is and I'm excited for him to show it at this level."

So while Saliba recovers from his injury on the back of a fourth PFA Team of the Year selection in a row, he may have a fight on his hands to displace Konsa when he returns to the Arsenal team.

Sports.title: What could trigger driver-market drama after new Verstappen, Norris deals?
Sports.content:
After a summer of speculation, contract extensions for Max Verstappen and Lando Norris suggest the elite seats on the Formula 1 grid are locked in for at least the next couple of years.

Four-time world champion Verstappen had been linked with a move to either Mercedes or McLaren but instead signed a Red Bull extension that ties him to the team until 2030.

There was little doubt that reigning world champion Norris' long-term future lay with McLaren, but team and driver made that official by announcing a multi-year extension on Saturday.

Meanwhile, it was perhaps the superb form of championship leader Kimi Antonelli that convinced Mercedes boss Toto Wolff he didn't need to poach Verstappen from Red Bull.

Given Wolff and Mercedes also manage Antonelli, there appears little doubt that he will remain with the Silver Arrows for many years to come. George Russell's situation is similar, and the Brit has repeatedly expressed his desire to remain with Mercedes.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch Lando Norris' roller-coaster season so far, which has seen several DNFs and race wins, putting him in the mix to challenge for the title.

Ferrari gave Charles Leclerc an extension in June, while Lewis Hamilton has insisted on several occasions this year that he has no plans to hang up his helmet any time soon.

With the line-ups of F1's 'big four' teams seemingly set for the short-term future, Sky Sports F1 examine when and how that situation could change.

Frustration for Russell or Piastri

While both Mercedes and McLaren have a track record of avoiding giving one driver priority status over the other, George Russell and Oscar Piastri are at risk of becoming seen as second fiddles.

Norris crucially came out on top of Piastri in the battle for last year's drivers' title, and has adapted to F1's new 2026 cars much faster than the Australian.

Russell started the year as the title favourite but has been clearly outperformed by Antonelli, with the Italian retaining huge amounts of room for improvement having only turned 20 last week.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Following Max Verstappen's Red Bull contract extension, George Russell and Lando Norris respond to questions about whether he ever posed a threat or caused concern.

Both Piastri and Russell will retain belief that they can turn the tables on their team-mates, next season if not during the remainder of their current campaigns, but there is no guarantee that will be achieved.

In the event either driver continues to be consistently outperformed over the next 18 months, they might begin to feel that their prospects of winning a maiden championship would ultimately be improved by a switch of team.

Hamilton retires

Hamilton has insisted he plans to be around for a while yet, but it remains to be seen how long the 41-year-old will continue in F1.

He's understood to have an option in his current deal to drive for the team until the end of the 2028 season, which would take him to the brink of his 44th birthday.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player 41-year-old Lewis Hamilton plans to remain in Formula One for quite some time to come.

While Fernando Alonso continues to amaze by competing in F1 at the age of 45, the Spaniard's example is far from the norm, and Hamilton driving beyond 2028 would be surprising to many.

That means there is a decent chance a Ferrari seat opens up for the 2029 season, if not earlier.

Britain's Oliver Bearman, who has been loaned out to Haas from the Ferrari junior programme, is a candidate from within, but the opportunity to drive in the Italian team's iconic red will always attract interest from just about every driver on the grid.

Red Bull remain off the pace

Red Bull have convinced Verstappen to sign a contract extension until 2030, but both team and driver refused to confirm whether the new deal includes the sort of exit clauses that have created so much chatter around the Dutchman's future for the last couple of years.

There's little doubt that Verstappen won't be content accepting the level of performance his team are currently producing, with Red Bull lagging behind Mercedes, Ferrari and McLaren.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player A 360-degree look at Max Verstappen’s race-ending crash at the Dutch Grand Prix on Sunday.

The 28-year-old is clearly going to give the Milton Keynes squad the chance to get back in the mix next year, but should they fail to do so, chatter will inevitably resume around potential alternative options for 2028.

We're already aware that Mercedes and McLaren engaged in talks over signing Verstappen at various stages over the last couple of years, so those channels of communication are open.

And if Hamilton were to decide to retire, there is little doubt that Ferrari would join the list of potential suitors.

Aston Martin break up 'big four'

Another factor that could shake up the driver market would be a team breaking up the dominance of the sport's established top four teams.

Several teams saw the introduction of both new power unit and chassis regulations in 2026 as an opportunity to make a jump, but the top four has been unchanged.

The team with perhaps the biggest aspirations were Aston Martin, but they have woefully underdelivered, and it remains to be seen how quickly Honda can get its troublesome power unit up to speed.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Aston Martin team principal Adrian Newey is optimistic their recent upgrades will boost the performance of the cars.

If Honda were somehow able to have their engine in the same ballpark as the leading manufacturers by the start of next season, few would bet against Aston Martin team principal Adrian Newey overseeing a chassis design up there with the best on the grid.

If Aston Martin, or any other team, somehow became a contender for race wins sooner rather than later, there would be another serious option for the drivers currently occupying the sport's most-wanted seats.

Sports.title: 'My body started to collapse' - Djokovic falls at first hurdle in shock US Open exit
Sports.content:
Novak Djokovic fell at the first hurdle as his tilt at a record-breaking 25th Grand Slam came to a shocking end to Argentine Mariano Navone in a five-set marathon at the US Open.

The 39-year-old went down 7-6 (7-5) 5-7 4-6 6-2 6-1 to the world No 49 in a match that lasted four hours and 36 minutes.

It was the longest opening match of a Grand Slam in Djokovic's career and the earliest exit at a major since the 2006 Australian Open.

With victory over Novak Djokovic, Mariano Navone has now...

✅ become the first player to defeat Djokovic in the first round at the US Open



✅ become the first to defeat Djokovic in the first round at a Grand Slam since Paul Goldstein (Australian Open 2006)



✅ claimed a first Top 10 win at Grand Slams



Navone ended the Serbian's bid for a fifth US Open title as he struggled with physical problems in ‌oppressive humidity.

The Serbian was 42-12 in five-set matches, while Navone was 0-4 but Djokovic was unable to battle through as he struggled to move at times and vomited on multiple occasions.

With this defeat, the question now lingers as to whether this was Djokovic's final match at this or any Grand Slam.

"I didn't enjoy myself," Djokovic said. "I think it was obvious that it was an awful feeling on the court for me.

"It's something that I've been carrying, unfortunately, pretty much every match this year. Vomiting, throwing up, a serious issue there. Then my whole body started to collapse, basically cramping and pain.

"The back just gave up in the end and shoulder, and I couldn't close it out. Can the issue be fixed? I don't know. I'm trying, man. I'm trying. Let's see."

Elsewhere, American Sofia Kenin held off a second-set fightback from compatriot Venus Williams, winning a ‌tie-break to complete a 6-2 7-6(6) victory over the two-time US Open champion.

The match began at 12.13 am at Arthur Ashe Stadium which marked the latest starting women's match in US Open history.

How an ailing Djokovic crashed out at Flushing Meadows...

Image: Djokovic gestures to the crowd after exiting the US Open

The last time the Serbian great had been seen on a tennis court, in Cincinnati two weeks ago, he was collapsing to his knees and being sick into a towel.

After that defeat by Thiago Tirante, Djokovic revealed he had a "health issue" which he has been dealing with "for many years", and which affects him in heat and humidity.

It was certainly warm in New York but by no means Cincinnati levels, yet Djokovic's cheeks were already red and his hair drenched in sweat midway through the first set, which he had led 3-0 but lost in a tie-break.

Having already successfully lobbied to have the roof closed, and with his wife, Jelena, and kids watching from the stands, Djokovic hit back late in the second set - after throwing up by the courtside towel box - with the crucial break for 6-5 and then serving it out.

He was sick again midway through the third - despite the air conditioning switched on - but still took his one chance to break serve as he moved one set away from victory.

Djokovic vomited again at the start of the fourth before breaking once more for 2-1, but Navone - a 25-year-old from Argentina who earlier this year won his first ATP singles title - did not go away.

After firing a shot wide in the fourth set, Djokovic landed awkwardly and dropped his racket before all but conceding the fourth set.

Is the greatest era of men’s tennis is fading?

This is the first time that we haven’t seen Novak Djokovic, Roger Federer, or Rafael Nadal in the second round of a Grand Slam since 2003



23 years



Djokovic appeared to be cramping up and he could barely move as Navone struck back, winning just one more game in a dramatic defeat.

The Serbian, who was holding back tears at one point in the fifth set, ended up making 70 unforced errors in a painful performance that ended minutes before midnight in New York.

"I was a break up in the fourth, but just struggled all the way since the fourth game of the match," he added.

"I don't want to take too much out of his win. Congrats to him. He's a nice guy, a fighter. But, you know, I didn't enjoy myself.

"When it comes to the match itself and the overall feeling of how I felt with my body and playing, it was really not enjoyable. I pretty much despised every moment that I spent on the court for that."

He will fall out of the top 10 of the ATP rankings for the first time in eight years.

Tale of the Tape: Navone vs Djokovic

Image: Navone revelled in the biggest win of his career

"It was very tough for me because you are playing with the 'GOAT' on this court," said Navone, who idolised Djokovic growing up.

"For sure it's the best thing I've had on court. This is an amazing court and the biggest stage. It's amazing, the way we play. I mean, five sets. I'm very happy. I don't know. What can I say?"

Sports.title: 'It's all there for them' - Root challenges England bowlers to 'create legacy'
Sports.content:
Joe Root has challenged his England team to carve out their own legacy in the game, after his side secured a series victory against Pakistan at Lord's.

The England captain described the victory as a "wonderful start" to his second spell in charge, with the result marking the side's first Test series win in a series of more than three matches since they beat New Zealand 2-1 away from home in December 2024

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Root called upon his players to carve out a legacy

Much of the pre-match conversation had centred on England's recent off-field issues, after fast bowler Brydon Carse was dropped for the second Test against Pakistan following an incident outside a Derby nightclub last week.

In trying batting conditions at Lord's, England beat Pakistan by 194 runs, after setting the visitors a huge target of 389 to win, with Dan Lawrence bringing up a second-innings half-century, while Emilio Gay and Harry Brook both battled to scores of 31 and 34, respectively.

England's four-pronged pace attack excelled on an unpredictable Lord's pitch, with Ollie Robinson, the pick of the bowlers and the Player of the Match, taking a whopping eight wickets across both of Pakistan's innings, while Jofra Archer and Josh Tongue also taking five wickets each.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ollie Robinson was crowned the Player of the Match after taking eight wickets across two innings

While praising his players, Root looked to the future and urged his team to keep showcasing their skill in different conditions around the world.

"This is a group of players that's going to be around this team for a long period of time and has a real opportunity to influence and shape it, both on and off the field," Root said.

"The two performances we've put forward have been a really good step in the right direction.

"We now have the chance to go and do that again at Edgbaston in whatever conditions we find ourselves in and then we'll move forward again to the next challenge when we go to South Africa.

"The more we can play together and the more we understand how we're going to operate in different conditions, the more we'll grow and the better we'll be for it. That's both for me as a captain and for them, learning and developing as Test players.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Root said he was pleased with how his side performed in the trying conditions

"The challenge will be a new set of conditions to handle. Can we be good enough or skilful enough to find the answers again?"

While Robinson exploited the turning Lord's pitch to extract plenty of lateral movement, he was complemented by the ferocious pace of Gus Atkinson, Tongue and Archer, the latter reaching an incredible 94mph in the first innings.

"The most exciting thing about these guys is they have the opportunity to create their own legacy," Root said.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Josh Tongue took three wickets, notably dismissing Saud Shakeel for 97 runs

"They're all of an age where they can play together for a long period of time, and I think they've all got skill sets that travel around the world in different conditions.

"It's all there for them if they keep working hard and performing in the manner that they are now, then there's no reason why they can't write their own little chapter in English fast bowling history."

'Conditions were challenging'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Eoin Morgan reacts to the MCC's proposed improvements of the Lord's pitch

Reflecting on the performances of his batters, Root hailed Lawrence and Gay for their second-innings scores in tough batting conditions.

He added Gay, who was pinned lbw by a low bouncing ball from Mohammad Abbas, was "very unlucky" to be removed.

"I'm thrilled for the guys that have managed to find a way of scoring in these conditions; it's been really hard," he said.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mohammad Abbas produced a low, skidding delivery to trap Emilio Gay lbw

Lord's has found itself back in the spotlight again this week for how its pitch has played, with 21 wickets falling during the match to lbw and bowled deliveries.

The pitch received an 'unsatisfactory' rating from the ICC after the New Zealand Test in June, and today, The MCC has unveiled an Action Plan of how they hope to improve the wicket going forward.

Root, however, believes the Dukes ball has also been part of the issue.

"I know The Home of Cricket is desperate to produce the best surface possible and I'm sure they're doing everything they can to provide that moving forward.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ollie Robinson trapped Azan Awais lbw for six before bowling Abdullah Shafique for a duck three balls later

"I think the balls have been very different this year," he added. "I think there's a different lacquer on them, I've not got evidence on that and probably need to ask Dukes, but I think there's a lacquer on the seam. They don't want them to go out of shape.

"I think that they are affecting the wickets; I think they're dinting more, and as a batter, when you practise, they're cracking your bats more frequently. They seem a lot firmer and probably if they're dinting the wickets and then it's going to seam off the dints as well."

'I like to think I have a big score around the corner'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Nasser Hussain and Michael Atherton discuss the reasons behind Root's recent vulnerability to lbw dismissals

On an individual level, Root was trapped lbw by Abbas for four runs in England's first innings, before being pinned by Mohammad Ali for 24 runs in the second.

"I'd love to have scored more runs," Root said, reflecting on his own game. "But when you're winning games, it's important to see things for what they are.

"I think the reason I've got the runs that I have in Test cricket is I've always been quite good at being level and eventually problem-solving.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Root was trapped twice lbw in both innings, but says he is calm about where his game is at

"I'll continue to keep working hard, I might have been out lbw a few times. Some of those have been on umpire's call, which, if they go the other way, might not be as much of a talking point.

"We've also seen the ball move more than it ever has. Three of my lbw dismissals have been here at Lord's where it seems significantly.

"I think there has to be a sense of calm and realism about things, but also I'll continue to keep working at my game, improving it and I know I'm a good player. I like to think there's a big score around the corner."

Sports.title: Donald ends retirement to make dramatic Rams return
Sports.content:
Aaron Donald has officially come out of retirement and will return for the Los Angeles Rams this season.

The 35-year-old is coming back after two and a half years away from the game to form a defensive pairing with Myles Garrett that will alarm every offensive line in the NFL.

The Rams confirmed Donald's decision on Sunday at the end of weeks of talks and almost two months of workouts at the club's facility, where Donald tested whether his body could stand another season. He has signed a one-year contract, with ESPN reporting the deal is worth at least $20m and built heavily on incentives.

Donald walked away without warning in March 2024 after 10 seasons spent entirely with the franchise in St Louis and Los Angeles, a career that brought three Defensive Player of the Year awards, 10 Pro Bowl selections, eight All-Pro honours and a Super Bowl ring, and established him as one of the defining defensive players of his generation.

It was the Rams' trade for Garrett this summer that set the comeback in motion. The former Cleveland Browns star has won two of the last three Defensive Player of the Year awards, meaning the new team-mates own five of the past nine between them.

They join a side already installed as favourites for a second Super Bowl under Sean McVay before Donald's return was even confirmed.

Matthew Stafford, the reigning MVP, leads a Rams offence that ranked first in the league and returns every major contributor, while cornerbacks Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson have arrived from Kansas City to strengthen the other side of the ball.

Donald's 111 career sacks remain a franchise record and the second-most in NFL history by a player operating primarily inside, where his ability to collapse pockets between the tackles drew constant double teams and created space for team-mates throughout his first decade.

Returning resets the clock on a Hall of Fame induction that had been due to become possible in 2029, a price Donald has accepted for the chance to chase a second ring alongside Garrett and a young supporting cast of Byron Young, Kobie Turner and Braden Fiske – starting with the season opener against the San Francisco 49ers in Australia next month.

Sports.title: Marcus Rashford’s Manchester United return feels like a marriage of convenience | Will Unwin
Sports.content:
The first chant of the match was for Marcus Rashford, Manchester United’s returning rogue son, the one banished for 18 months, first to the Midlands and then Catalonia. Every football fan loves an academy product who has risen up the ranks, from scrawny child to getting 76,000 off their seats. Rashford is one of these, living out the dream of everyone inside Old Trafford and they are willing to forgive but want something in return.

Not since 7 December 2024 has Rashford been seen in red at Old Trafford. Then it was as a substitute forlornly trying to turn things around in an eventual 3-2 defeat by Nottingham Forest. His relationship with Ruben Amorim was already deteriorating, the second head coach to have become irritated with Rashford. After loans with Aston Villa and Barcelona, everyone is surprised to see him back; it feels like a marriage of convenience because of a lack of offers and securing a replacement was deemed complex.

At Hull, Rashford came on at the break for Patrick Dorgu after a dispiriting 45 minutes but floundered down blind alleys as he tried to spark a listless team into action. The truth is, Michael Carrick needs someone of Rashford’s experience and quality to be at the forefront of this latest attempt of building a successful era. He cannot have any off-field misdemeanours or sulking on the pitch when things are tough.

Carrick is more willing to put an arm around the shoulder, understanding of the pressures that come with playing for United. That is increased when the situation is dire, being behind at home against a promoted club a week after being beaten by another. It is a test of character, one United have failed too often in recent times.

Rashford’s ability has never been doubted: this is someone who did not look out of place at Barcelona and spent the summer playing for his country at the World Cup. In the buildup to the tournament, he went away and worked privately, inviting former teammates to help him to train in Miami, showing a dedication to his craft.

At 28, he should be a leader and Carrick is giving him the opportunity to be one. United have the teenagers Shea Lacey and JJ Gabriel waiting for opportunities, and Rashford is someone they can learn from, having witnessed more than most. He started brightly against Ipswich on the left wing, with United eager to target Dara O’Shea on that side. Rashford can go either way, pushing past a defender to reach the byline or cut in. He tried both, creating dangerous situations with his crossing but without a striker capable of finding the finish.

While Bruno Fernandes, rightly, takes the headlines with his hat‑trick, everyone knows United cannot rely on one man, however influential he may be. Following Fernandes’s example has not always been part of the Rashford playbook but seeing his influence on a team should offer some inspiration for the England international to reach the levels he and United expect. Rashford was certainly not at his best but his head remained high, making runs into dangerous areas, even if the chances of reaching the ball were somewhat forlorn.

View image in fullscreen Bruno Fernandes (right) could be an inspiration to Marcus Rashford. Photograph: Dave Thompson/AP

Finishing without a goal or assist when five were scored may irk Rashford but reputations cannot be rebuilt completely in 80 minutes. Willingness needs to be the bare minimum because it will be a long season for United and everyone will need to play their part. On another day, Bryan Mbeumo would not have turned Rashford’s cross on to the bar from a yard out or his saved shot would have beaten the goalkeeper.

Against Hull, barely a clearcut chance was created as United fired blanks, but on Sunday, 33 shots were attempted, 11 of those on target. It was a display of greater intent, energy and productivity, but a long way from flawless as Ipswich were given chances to capitalise on. One reason United were able to cause problems in the second half was down to Rashford and Mbeumo being relentless, occupying defenders and, ultimately, tiring minds and legs with United in the ascendancy.
