“Really pleased with Marcus, I am sure it was nice for him to be back and start games and be involved in a good performance,” Carrick said. “I thought he did particularly well in not easy circumstances. I thought he did all round good and will only get better.”

Rashford is United’s No 9 in squad number only, as Carrick is opting to use Benjamin Sesko from the start. When the Slovene is fully fit, a different dimension will be added to the attack, a player used to finishing crosses, which will help Rashford – and others – to thrive. After a year alongside Robert Lewandowski, Rashford is used to having a clinical finisher waiting for service and having an out-and-out striker would benefit him.

Even if few expected Rashford and United to continue their alliance, they are back together. Harmony is not completely restored but both have shown they can make things work,; the affection is evident. The good times and the bad are remembered by both, from the debut goals against Midtjylland to the fallout with Amorim, Rashford’s United story is a rich tapestry, spanning his entire life, and it is not over yet.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta ‘begging’ Premier League to expand 20-man matchday squads
Sports.content:
Arsenal have asked the Premier League to increase the size of matchday squads, with Mikel Arteta saying the current system is detrimental to player welfare. Top‑flight clubs can name 20 players for games, including a minimum of three homegrown players. In Spain’s La Liga, clubs can name a matchday squad of 23, while Italy’s Serie A allows 25.

Arsenal have competed on multiple fronts in recent seasons. Last year, as well as winning the Premier League, they reached the finals of the Champions League and Carabao Cup, as well as the quarter-finals of the FA Cup. With pressure increasing on the football calendar and players facing more matches, Arteta sees no reason why English teams should operate with smaller squads than those from other European leagues.

“I’ve been begging the Premier League if we can extend those numbers just for the welfare of the players, which is the most important thing, because I think every squad needs more than 20 outfield players, ideally, to sustain the level of demand in international games that we have,” Arteta said, as he prepares for the champions’ trip to Aston Villa on Monday night. “But these are the rules, and within the rules we have to play. We need to be very close to the players to explain those situations in the right way, for everybody to feel important, because they will be.”

Clubs can register a squad of 25 senior players – those aged over 21 – for the season, with at least eight homegrown. As a result, five senior players registered for the season miss out each game. Arteta has said it can be difficult to tell players they are not involved and that the news can negatively affect their wellbeing.

“The question has to be to the players. What do they want? If they raise their hands and say: ‘No, I prefer to stay at home and not travel,’ I think we have an issue because then they don’t love what they do, which is the matchday,” he said. “But I’m sure that if you ask the players, everybody would like to be part of the squad on matchday, because that’s the way that they can fulfil themselves.

“Otherwise you have to tell somebody: ‘You are not even part of this matchday,’ and that’s really tough. And it doesn’t help anybody. It doesn’t help the club. It doesn’t help the valuation of the player. It doesn’t help the player feel part of something. It’s a real issue that has a really simple solution.”

Arteta added: “And all the clubs, because I’ve done the research with all the top clubs in Europe, we are not different to anybody. Most of them, 90% of them, they have more players than us. So we are going to have to deal with that.”

Sports.title: Aston Villa and Chelsea still enemies despite transfer pipeline, insists Emery
Sports.content:
Unai Emery has said Aston Villa and Chelsea are enemies rather than friends, insisting the clubs want to “kill” each other despite regularly doing business in recent years.

Emiliano Martínez became the latest player to move between the teams, after Chelsea paid £117m to sign Morgan Rogers from Villa this summer. Nicolas Jackson, who could become Villa’s record signing after joining in a deal worth up to £65m, and Alejandro Garnacho both joined Villa from Chelsea in this window, the latter on a loan deal with a conditional obligation to buy.

The fee for Rogers was a record for a British player, while the clubs agreed a £7.5m deal for Martínez, who for a second successive season expressed his desire to leave Villa Park. Austin MacPhee, the set-piece coach who was among a trio of Emery’s core staff to leave this summer, also joined Chelsea from Villa.

Last year, Villa signed Axel Disasi on loan from Chelsea and in 2024 paid £37.5m to sign Ian Maatsen permanently from the London club. Carney Chukwuemeka and Omari Kellyman, now of Borussia Dortmund and Strasbourg respectively, moved in the opposite direction in previous seasons, in 2022 and 2024 respectively.

Emery played down the notion that Villa enjoy good relations with Chelsea. “Good relations? The relationship is only through the deals – for money, for other players,” he said.

“They want to kill us. And we want to kill them … it is not a good relationship. Of course, because we have good players and we can as well sign players from them, but it’s not a good relationship, it’s a deal for money and a deal for players. And they will want to kill us. They are signing Morgan, they are signing Emiliano Martínez to kill us … I am happy for Emiliano Martínez, I am happy for Morgan Rogers and, of course, I know I am not happy for Chelsea.”

Villa, who host Arsenal on Monday hoping to bounce back from a chastening 4-0 defeat at Brighton, have outperformed Chelsea in recent seasons. Villa will play in the Champions League for the second time in three seasons, while Chelsea missed out on qualifying for European competition altogether last campaign.

Emery could hand Jackson, Leon Goretzka – who won the Champions League with Bayern Munich 2020 – and Zion Suzuki debuts at Villa Park. “I know we must rebuild the team,” Villa’s manager said.

View image in fullscreen Leon Goretzka (left) is set to make his Aston Villa debut against Arsenal. Photograph: Neville Williams/Aston Villa FC/Getty Images

“We will need time. But we must compete on Monday. We needed to compete last Sunday in Brighton but we didn’t compete. We are working every day as fast as possible to be ready, everybody.”

Emery, who spent 18 months in charge of Arsenal, praised the work of his successor, Mikel Arteta, and believes his former club are favourites to retain the Premier League and win the Champions League, a trophy that has eluded them. “Arsenal are the favourites,” the Basque said.

“Arsenal, looking at the team with Arteta there seven years in a row, are getting better and better and are investing more and more. They are getting bigger and bigger as a club with the players they can sign. Arteta is doing a fantastic job. Arsenal are the favourites to win the Premier League and to win the Champions League. I like watching them a lot.”

Emery said he is looking forward to the transfer window closing on Tuesday and conceded Villa’s preparations for the season were hampered by offers for key players. The exits of Martínez and Ollie Watkins to Al-Hilal mean six of Villa’s starting XI from their Europa League triumph in May will have left the club this summer.

“It doesn’t make sense to finish the transfer window on 1 September, and maybe for some teams like us, it’s more difficult, because when they are coming, more changes than normal, of course we are struggling to build a team to compete at the beginning of the season,” Emery said. “This year again I am wishing to finish the transfer window on 1 September and close the squad with the players I want.”

Sports.title: Women’s Super League 2026-27 preview No 10: London City Lionesses
Sports.content:
Guardian writers’ predicted position: 4th (NB: this is not necessarily Suzanne Wrack’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)

Last season’s position: 6th

Prospects

Trying to figure out what London City will look like this season, or where they will finish, is nigh on impossible. Eight players have come in as the owner, Michele Kang, bids to continue her drive towards the top of the Women’s Super League and there are some superstars in that group, among them the two-time Ballon d’Or winner Alexia Putellas.

The WSL debutants finished a respectable sixth last season, but were 22 points adrift of the top three. Evidence suggests Kang will be ruthless if the team do not meet her expectations – despite a strong start to the 2025-26 campaign, Jocelyn Prêcheur was sacked as manager shortly before Christmas and replaced by Eder Maestre.

Wholesale changes to teams hoping to break into the top three have proved costly in the past. The hope will be that the level of the players coming in will help London City develop into a side capable of securing Champions League football and challenging for the league. What is clear is that Kang’s spending and ambition is playing a big role in bringing some of the biggest players in the world to the WSL. Mapi León said of her: “Everything counts when you make this kind of a decision, and of course, she was an important part because seeing another woman doing so much to help women’s sports and women’s football grow, I think it’s impossible not to value that. I think it’s something very powerful.”

Off-field picture

London City’s accounts for 2024-25 showed an operating loss of £10.6m and the effect of their big spending before their first season in the WSL, and even bigger spending this summer, will show in future filings. The 2024-25 loss was more than 10 times their £902,000 revenue in that period. Critically, there is a need to grow the fanbase and, with no men’s club supporter pool to draw from, London City will have to be inventive.

The manager

Maestre was appointed in January having previously managed UD Tenerife in Liga F, guiding them to sixth. Maestre’s contract runs until 2028, but he cannot rest on that given Kang’s high expectations. The 42-year-old has shifted the way London City play and a host of new signings could prove fruitful in his system.

Star signing

Mary Earps, León and Kadidiatou Diani have arrived from Paris Saint-Germain, Barcelona and Lyonnes respectively, but it is the recruitment of Putellas that has rocked the WSL. The 32-year-old spent 14 years at Barcelona, helping them to the top of the women’s game, in the process becoming a talismanic figure. Putellas is far from past her prime and had the pick of clubs worldwide when deciding to leave Spain. Her recruitment was a statement of intent from Kang.

View image in fullscreen The 32-year-old Alexia Putellas has plenty to offer London City Lionesses. Photograph: Daniel Weir/Sports Press Photo/Shutterstock

Stat attack

London City made more Opta-defined defensive errors that led to goals and conceded more penalties than any other team in the WSL last season. Elene Lete saved one penalty and the players in front of the 24-year-old goalkeeper need to make her life easier.

Set for a breakthrough

Superstars have come through the door this summer, meaning Nicole Anyomi is one that has slipped under the radar and could go on to make a big impression. Anyomi is a little bit of an unknown to UK audiences having played all her club football in Germany. The forward scored 60 goals in 130 games for Frankfurt in five years. She also has four goals in 34 games for Germany.

What they say

“I’m going to bring to the project whatever the project needs from me, so I’m 100% committed. I’m hungry to win, to be better day after day, to fight with my teammates for the victory” – Putellas

Where are they playing their home games?

Hayes Lane in Bromley is far from an ideal ground for such an ambitious club given the 5,150 capacity. The medium- to long-term goal is to upsize, but space for a ground in and around London is limited. Before any move, however, London City need to increase their fanbase.

Sports.title: Transfer roundup: Ollie Watkins completes move to Al-Hilal from Aston Villa
Sports.content:
Al-Hilal have signed Ollie Watkins from Aston Villa, ⁠the two clubs announced on Sunday, as the 30-year-old striker ended a successful ⁠six-year spell with ⁠the ​Midlands club where he became their top scorer in the Premier League. The England international, who had ​two years left on ‌his Villa contract, has moved for a reported £51m.

Watkins ‌signed a three-year contract as Al-Hilal acquired ‌a proven goalscorer after he scored 21 goals in all competitions last season, including five goals in the Europa League as he helped deliver a European trophy to Unai Emery’s side.

However, an ‌exit was on the cards before the transfer window closed, with Emery revealing the ​striker had apologised for making himself unavailable for the club’s Premier League opener, a 4-0 defeat at Brighton.

Watkins scored 91 Premier League goals for Villa and 108 ⁠in all competitions since arriving from Brentford for £28m in ​2020. The striker is among ​a string of departures from Villa ​in the ‌close season following ​the ​exits of key players such as Morgan Rogers and Emi Martinez to Chelsea – the latter moving on Sunday – Ezri Konsa to Arsenal and Youri Tielemans to Manchester United.

Quick Guide How do I 

Roma have stepped up their Serie A challenge with the acquisition of two captains, midfielder Marten De Roon coming over from Atalanta and centre-back Leonardo Balerdi joining from Marseille. The 35-year-old De Roon evolved into Atalanta’s skipper after a decade spent in Bergamo over two spells. He will reunite with Roma’s manager Gian Piero Gasperini, who formerly coached him at Atalanta.

And the former Serie A MVP Rafael Leão has completed a €38m transfer from Milan to Galatasaray. The Turkish side confirmed a deal for the Portugal winger, signing him to a four-year contract with a net salary of €10m per season.

Sports.title: Chelsea hold off Brighton in 4-3 win but remain chaotic under Xabi Alonso
Sports.content:
In the fullness of time Chelsea’s surrender against Brighton in April may be seen as the turning point. The humiliation accelerated Liam ­Rosenior’s demise and forced the Stamford Bridge hierarchy into a ­reckoning leading to the appointment of Xabi Alonso, a shift in ­transfer ­strategy, the birth of the JP Morgan front three and the end of ­Robert Sánchez’s time in goal.

For now, though, the argument that Emiliano Martínez is the final piece in the jigsaw seems a touch ­premature. With seven goals scored and five conceded while winning their first two league games, it is not hard to see where Chelsea need to improve in order to sustain a title challenge. They have to be savvier when ahead, and although the good has so far outweighed the bad Alonso could do with his side not dropping their guard when they have the ­opposition on the ropes.

Alonso’s cool disappeared as ­Chelsea’s focus dipped after they went 3-0 up against an injury‑hit Brighton inside 32 minutes. ­Stamford Bridge was anxious when a João Pedro own‑goal cut the ­advantage to one just after the hour. Alonso was ­shouting at his bench and it was only when Cole Palmer scored with 16 minutes left that calm was restored.

View image in fullscreen Xabi Alonso has won his first two league games as Chelsea manager, but neither have been what you would call relaxing. Photograph: David Klein/Reuters

Not for long, mind you, given that Brighton still managed to grab a consolation through Pascal Gross deep into added time.

It was that kind of game, Martínez conceding three despite playing well on his debut after joining from Aston Villa for £7.5m. “We can hurt teams,” the Argentina goalkeeper said. “At the back, we need to bring the goals down.”

Alonso agreed. Chelsea have been thrilling in transition – they beat Fulham with 37% possession last Monday and had only 26% against Brighton – but they must tighten up when they visit Arsenal next Sunday.

Equally, few sights will be more captivating this season than Palmer combining with João Pedro and ­Morgan Rogers in attack. Palmer looks refreshed after a summer off and Chelsea will be dangerous when games turn into shootouts. They have so many ways to score. The hope is that there will be more stability with Martínez in position.

Alonso did not hesitate to start Martínez, even though the ­Argentinian lacks match ­practice and joined on Friday. “He felt ready,” Alonso said of Martínez, the first 30‑something player to start for ­Chelsea since ­Thiago Silva in May 2024. “We will feel his ­presence because he has this charisma, this aura to influence.”

Chelsea, again in a 3-4-2-1 system, are getting serious. Sánchez was not even on the bench against his old side and needs to leave. There was a huge ovation for Martínez before kick‑off and it was followed by the focus switching to Brighton’s No 1 in the fourth minute, a handling error from Bart Verbruggen allowing Roméo Lavia to put Chelsea ahead after Mats Wieffer had cleared a João Pedro header off the line from a corner.

It was a lovely moment for Lavia. It was four years to the day since the Belgian’s last goal, against Chelsea coincidentally enough. His luck with injuries is hopefully turning.

View image in fullscreen Roméo Lavia was on hand to punish Bart Verbruggen’s early handling error and put Chelsea 1-0 up. Photograph: Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC/Getty Images

Lavia starting his second consecutive league game was important with Chelsea light in midfield. Moisés Caicedo limped off after coming on in the second half, Reece James started on the bench and Enzo ­Fernández was off ­pining for a move to ­Manchester City, so Malo Gusto moved in from right wing-back to partner Lavia.

Chelsea’s selection issues were nothing compared to Brighton’s problems, though. Fabian Hürzeler did not use the absence of Jack Hinshelwood, Yasin Ayari, Georginio Rutter, Kaoru Mitoma and Yankuba Minteh as an excuse, but it had an impact.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Chelsea were rampant. Rogers ­continued his fine start after joining from Villa, creating the second goal with a powerful surge away from Luka Vuskovic in the 14th ­minute. Brighton were caught cold by a throw‑in and Rogers crossed for Pedro Neto to score.

Linked with a move away this summer, Neto has been repurposed by Alonso as a wing-back and was bright. João Pedro missed a chance after strong pressing from the ­Portugal international. The away end jeered but João Pedro converted his next opportunity, when a Rogers flick sent Jorrel Hato flying down the left to set the former Brighton striker up.

View image in fullscreen João Pedro rather summed up Chelsea’s start under Xabi Alonso with a goal, an assist and an own goal. Photograph: Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC/Getty Images

Chelsea’s mistake was thinking it was over. Brighton responded before half‑time, Malick Yalcouyé ­volleying in after Martínez made a brave block from ­Charalampos ­Kostoulas. “They showed belief in their quality,” ­Hürzeler said of his players.

The German thought Brighton deserved more. Chelsea were wobbling when João Pedro diverted a Gross cross past Martínez. Diego Gómez then lashed a shot wide and Martínez denied Olivier Boscagli the equaliser.

Alonso needed his big players to step up. Palmer, who had earlier sidefooted over from close range, delivered when he took a João Pedro flick and bent a shot past Verbruggen. Chelsea will be anything but dull.

Sports.title: Calvert-Lewin cancels out Schade’s opener as Leeds salvage point against Brentford
Sports.content:
These nascent moments of the new season can often provide false hope but, as both sets of players shook hands after what was indisputably the correct result at Elland Road, it was difficult not to imagine we had just witnessed a contest between two sides that should have lofty ­ambitions for the months ahead.

Leeds and Brentford were vic­torious on the opening weekend in differing circumstances. Leeds crafted a hard-earned but ultimately deserved win at Nottingham Forest, while Brentford Tottenham. Time will tell what the ceiling of both these sides is but, as they each continued their unbeaten starts here, hopes should be high.

This was a thoroughly ­entertaining game but it was also an occasion in which both managers, as well as the players, displayed their importance to their respective clubs.

Managers are scrutinised at every turn but Daniel Farke and Keith Andrews both excelled here. Both have had question marks as to whether they were the right man to take their team forward: Andrews when he was surprisingly appointed just over a year ago, and Farke in the difficult early stages of last season.

Andrews’s tactical nous was at its peak in the first half. He nullified the Leeds back five and his team led at half-time and probably should have been more than a single goal in front. Kevin Schade’s wonderful flick to turn home a Keane Lewis-Potter cross was the least the visitors deserved.

However, Farke showed his own tactical flexibility at the break. The German was under immense pressure last November and at real risk of losing his job before a move to a back five away at Manchester City proved the catalyst to transform Leeds’s season. He did the reverse here, going back to a four and matching Brentford in the second half to great effect.

Spearheaded by the impact of Ao Tanaka and Lukas Nmecha, both on as substitutes, the hosts were the stronger of the two sides after half‑time. They ultimately got the equaliser their play deserved when ­Nmecha’s shot across goal was prodded home by Dominic Calvert-Lewin to ensure it would be a point apiece, and four from the first two for both sides.

The early evidence overall? Leeds and Brentford should both be ­looking upwards this season. “It’s definitely a good point,” Farke said. “It was a very difficult and complicated game like we expected. Brentford were ­excellent in the first half and deserved to be in the lead, but I’m so proud of our reaction.”

His side struggled to get to grips with Brentford’s shape in the first half. Ethan Ampadu and Anton Stach were overrun in midfield, with the visitors’ three of Vitaly Janelt, ­Mamadou ­Sangaré and ­Mikkel Damsgaard ­running riot. James ­Trafford was called into action on multiple occasions, with smart saves to deny Igor Thiago and Schade.

Such was the strength of Brentford’s momentum that a goal felt inevitable. It duly arrived as half‑time approached when Lewis-Potter’s cross caught the Leeds backline off‑guard and Schade, with his back to goal, turned the ball home expertly to silence Elland Road.

As mentioned, perhaps the ­biggest gripe at that stage was that ­Brentford’s lead wasn’t greater. “I thought we could have done more in the first half,” Andrews said.

“We could have tested Trafford more but we were outstanding. The storm was always going to come and they were forced into ­making changes they haven’t done for quite some time.”

Those changes were pivotal. The back five was abandoned, with Leeds adding Tanaka as an extra man in midfield. It provided an instant impact, with the balance of play shifting the way of the hosts. James Justin forced a clever save from Caoimhín Kelleher before Dan James, on as a substitute, arguably could have done better after being set free on halfway.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

In contrast, Brentford were struggling without as much space in the middle, with Igor Thiago cutting a slightly isolated and frustrated ­figure. The Leeds supporters, sensing the momentum was now with them, were beginning to come alive – as were their team. Just like in the first half, a goal was starting to feel more like an inevitability than a possibility.

Farke tweaked things further, with ­Nmecha pro­viding direct support for Calvert‑Lewin, and the duo combined with 11 ­minutes ­remaining. Nmecha dragged a shot across goal to leave Kelleher flat‑footed, with Calvert‑Lewin ­poking into the empty net for his first of the season.

A draw was the least Leeds deserved. Both sides showed their ambition by pushing for a winner, though they cancelled each other out in the final moments to underline further that these are two teams who should think positively about what lies ahead.

Sports.title: European football: Bellingham sparks Real Madrid’s cruise to maintain perfect start
Sports.content:
Real Madrid maintained their perfect start to the season in La Liga with a comfortable 4-0 home ⁠win over promoted Málaga on Sunday, scoring three times inside 30 minutes before adding a late fourth.

Jude Bellingham’s brilliant solo opener, an own ⁠goal by the Málaga goalkeeper, ⁠Alfonso Herrero, and ​a sharp Kylian Mbappé volley in effect settled the contest before half-time, with the substitute Arda Guler wrapping up the victory in added time at ⁠the Bernabéu.

The win lifted Madrid to nine points from three matches, two clear of Atlético Madrid and Alavés. Barcelona, fourth on six points with a ⁠game in hand, host Rayo Vallecano on Monday.

Bellingham opened the scoring in the 19th minute ‌with a superb burst through the middle, collecting a loose ball near the edge of the area, gliding past three defenders and firing low beneath Herrero. They ​doubled their lead seven minutes later after Herrero could only palm out Mbappé’s effort. Bellingham headed the rebound back towards goal and, as Herrero and a teammate collided while trying to clear, the ball ended up in the net.

Mbappé then made it 3-0 in the 30th minute, meeting Trent Alexander-Arnold’s cross ⁠with a fine volley from the centre of the box. The second half drifted until Guler, shortly ​after coming on, started ‌and finished a ​slick move, feeding Vinícius Júnior before tapping in the Brazilian’s return pass to complete the rout.

Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang scored for the third straight game as Deportivo La Coruña beat Valencia 3-1. The former Arsenal and Chelsea forward, who joined Deportivo from Marseille in the off-season, scored his side’s second goal as the newly promoted side won for the first time this season.

Napoli suffered a 2-1 defeat at home to Como ⁠in Serie A, with all three goals coming in an entertaining opening half. Assane Diao looked the most threatening player in the opening stages ⁠and the winger was instrumental in the visitors’ 17th-minute opening goal. Diao went past ​Mathías Olivera on the right wing ‌and played a pass ‌across to Martin Baturina whose shot on the turn from close to the penalty ‌spot found the bottom corner of the net.

View image in fullscreen Tasos Douvikas scores Como’s second goal against Napoli. Photograph: Giuseppe Maffia/NurPhoto/Shutterstock

Noa Lang missed an excellent chance to equalise, sending a header over from inside the six-yard box, before Napoli drew level on the half-hour mark. Rasmus Højlund collected a pass on the edge of the area and drilled the ball low into the far corner, but Como were back in front four minutes later when Napoli ​were caught napping at the back.

André-Frank Zambo Anguissa underhit a pass back to Amir Rrahmani in his own box, allowing Baturina to nick the ball away. It fell to Tasos Douvikas and Como’s top scorer last season netted his second goal of this ⁠campaign.

Hakan Calhanoglu’s early strike earned Inter a 1-0 win at Cagliari as they continued a perfect start to their title defence. The Turkey midfielder guided home a first-time strike from the edge of the box after nine minutes to make it two goals in two games and set the tone for a first half dominated by the champions in Sardinia.

Curtis Jones made his Inter debut from the bench in the second half, but Inter’s lack of composure in front of goal almost came back to bite them as Cagliari threatened a shock equaliser with a flurry of late chances.

Paris Brunner netted a goal in each half as Monaco beat visiting ⁠Marseille 2-0 to go top of Ligue 1 as the only team to win their first two games.

Monaco ⁠took the lead in the 13th minute when the Marseille defence was caught ball-watching as Brunner leaped between two defenders ⁠to head home a cross from Aleksandr Golovin. Marseille controlled the ball for long ​spells but struggled to create ‌shots on target, with ‌their efforts often blocked by the home side’s resolute rearguard.

Quick Guide Play our football trivia game, On the ball Show The Guardian's daily football game, On the ball, is now live in the app for both iOS and Android. Can you identify the Premier League star from the clues? Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Timothy Weah came close ‌to equalising for the visitors in the 53rd minute with a powerful shot from a tight angle that hit the side netting. It was to prove a costly miss as Brunner latched on to a long ball a minute later, speeding away from the defence before nonchalantly cutting ‌inside and slotting the ball in at the far post to make it 2-0.

Yuito Suzuki scored a hat-trick as Freiburg thumped Werder Bremen 4-1, while Schalke’s first game back in ⁠the Bundesliga ended in a 3-0 defeat at Augsburg as they finished with 10 men.

Sports.title: US Open star melts down with trainer who REFUSES to treat 'cramp' during medical timeout
Sports.content:
See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

French tennis star Terence Atmane was embroiled in a furious spat with US Open medical staff after he was refused treatment under the sport's strict rules around cramps.

Players are unable to take medical timeouts during matches if they suffer cramps and can only seek treatment briefly during changeovers or set breaks.

But Atmane was keen to stress that he was suffering from muscular pain separate from cramping - despite having struggled with the issue earlier in his five-set battle against Jaume Munar.

Calling for the physio deep in the fifth set, Atmane became incensed that he was being misunderstood by the responding physiotherapist as they questioned why he needed a medical timeout.

'I need treatment here, this is not cramping,' the 24-year-old said. 'This is pain. I have pain.

'I'm telling you, I have pain. On both sides, before I was cramping, and now I have pain. You don't understand? No, you don't understand. I need treatment, I really need treatment right now.'

Terence Atmane boiled over after he was refused a medical timeout after being deemed to have suffered cramp by the physio

The Frenchman had previously been treated in a break in play but continued to struggle with 'pain' in the fifth set

When told that he could not be treated if he was suffering cramp, Atmane turned up the volume.

'This was not cramp, it's pain. It was pain,' he raged. 'Excuse me, can you please give me treatment, and stop acting stupid. Is it possible to have some common sense? I tell him I have pain, why is he telling me no? I have pain.'

The tournament supervisor, called onto court to attend to the issue, urged Atmane to remember that the physio was a 'medical professional'.

'It's my body. I have pain on both there, so I need treatment there,' Atmane replied, before speaking over the physio.

'What do you mean come on man? I'm telling you I have pain on both my legs. P-A-I-N,' Atmane spelled out. 'Pain. Not cramp. I know the rules, that's why I'm asking you. It's not a cramp, it's pain.'

Despite his protestations, Atmane was refused treatment, but was unable to take no for an answer as the physio walked away.

'Come back, come back,' he called. 'What's your credentials? I don't know your name. No, no no, come back.'

Atmane then rounded on the umpire as he was ordered to return to play, adding: 'I have pain, and the guy says no. I'm telling him I have pain, and the guy says no. What does it matter? I get the name after this.'

During the third set, Atmane became so badly impaired with a muscular issue that he was almost unable to move

The 24-year-old was only able to serve underarm and lost the set 6-1 after building a strong two-set lead

Earlier in the match, Atmane was suffering so severely he was forced into limited movement and underarm serving in the third set.

The Frenchman was two sets up against the Spaniard when he began to struggle, and first received medical timeout for a leg issue, before continuing to play impaired.

Munar disagreed with the decision to award Atmane a timeout, and later accused Atmane of time-wasting and receiving extra on-court coaching, calling for the supervisor to complain directly.

Atmane went on to receive a time violation for repeatedly taking too much time between points.

World No. 55 Munar complained about his opponent's conduct again in the fifth set after Atmane's rant, but the pair exchanged a civil - if curt - handshake after Munar beat his rival 6-7(5), 3-6, 6-1, 7-6(4), 7-5.

Speaking to Daily Mail Sport after the match, Atmane said: 'It's very simple. I told (the physio) I had pain on my leg after the cramp, and then he told me that that was not true, and it was cramp.

'So I told him that what he was saying was not true because I had pain, and then he didn't want to treat me. So then after he left, simple as that. There's nothing I can do about it.

'I told him it was pain and not cramp because I was cramping before and it was like different kind of pain, and he didn't want it to treat me. So I said to him like, I mean, there's no point to fight. So that's it.

The drama on Court 13 throws into perspective the cloudiness which surrounds the rule, with the guidelines often criticised for inconsistent enforcement.

Cramps are classified as a fitness issue, rather than injury or illness, with many players turning to esoteric methods like drinking pickle juice on-court to stave off the dehydration often at the root of the problem.

But at this year's Australian Open, a tussle between Carlos Alcaraz and Alexander Zverev over the former's on-court treatment turned ugly with the German accusing the tournament of not adhering to the regulations.

The Career Grand Slam winner had been badly affected by the challenging heat in Melbourne, throwing up multiple times during their semi-final.

His movement was later affected, and Alcaraz went on to request a medical timeout, which was granted.

'He has cramps,' Zverev told the supervisor as Alcaraz received treatment. 'What else should it be? This is absolute bulls***.'

'That is unbelievable. That can not be. You can not be serious,' he continued in a mixture of German and English.

But Atmane said that he did not advocate for a change in the regulations, despite his experience on Sunday.

'I think that's fair that we cannot receive treatment when we have cramps,' Atmane added. 'I feel like it has always been like this, so I don't see why it should change.

'Even if today I was fully cramping, I never asked for the physio at that time. I feel like rules are rules, and we should respect them. It was a little bit unfortunate that he didn't wanted to treat the problem that I had, but it is what it is. At the end of the day, I lost, and it happened.'

Sports.title: Chelsea and Aston Villa are turning into the Premier League's greatest swap shop and it looks like the Blues are getting the better deal - but here's why the trades suit BOTH parties... and how Unai Emery can get the best out of Nicolas Jackson
Sports.content:
Chelsea and Aston Villa are turning into the Premier League's greatest swap shop and it looks like the Blues are getting the better deal - but here's why the trades suit BOTH parties... and how Unai Emery can get the best out of Nicolas Jackson

Unlock more from inside the Aston Villa camp with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight, analysis and more

The name Omari Kellyman probably means relatively little to most Premier League fans yet the young attacking midfielder is a crucial figure in relations between two of its most prominent clubs.

Two summers ago, Kellyman moved from Aston Villa to Chelsea for £19million. It seemed a high fee for a player who had made only six first-team appearances.

Blues academy product Ian Maatsen moved in the opposite direction for £37.5m and has played 91 times for Villa, though he has rarely been first choice at left-back. Kellyman, 20, moved to Strasbourg this month having never played a first-team game for Chelsea.

Summer 2024 was a time of widespread panic about the Premier League’s profitability and sustainability rules, as clubs scrambled to avoid possible points deductions. There is no suggestion of anything untoward on the part of either club, though Villa and Chelsea were warned by UEFA in summer 2025 that they were looking closely at so-called ‘swaps’.

Both are currently on the naughty step with European football chiefs having been fined in summer 2025 and are having to follow strict financial rules.

Omari Kellyman in pre-season action for Chelsea against Spurs this summer

Which brings us to the current window. Nicolas Jackson’s £65m switch from Stamford Bridge to Villa is the fourth transfer between the clubs since Morgan Rogers completed his £117million move to Chelsea on July 21. Villa need a centre-back before the window closes and as Chelsea have too many, the story may not end here.

At his press conference on Friday, Villa boss Unai Emery said Chelsea and Villa wanted to ‘kill’ each other on the pitch. Off it, though, the clubs seem to enjoy a healthier relationship.

The movers and shakers...

Villa co-owner Nassef Sawiris and his Chelsea counterpart Behdad Eghbali are decisive operators and if the people in charge can pick up the phone to one another, negotiations tend to move more quickly.

‘Both are operating under UEFA cost control sanctions and have to follow a business plan,’ said football finance expert Kieran Maguire.

‘The two clubs traded Maatsen and Kellyman in 2024 in a deal that made profits for both under Premier League rules, but not those of UEFA.’

Emery, however, gave short shrift to suggestions of co-operation. ‘Good relations?’ he said. ‘The relationship is only through deals for money. They want to kill us, and we want to kill them. We have players and we can sign their players but they’re deals for money and players. They signed Morgan and Emiliano Martinez to kill us.’

At least two weeks before Rogers’ move to Chelsea was announced, Daily Mail Sport understands that that possible transfer was being talked about openly in Premier League dressing rooms.

Emiliano Martinez's arrival was announced on Sunday before the visit of Brighton

Similarly, Villa had been chasing wide attackers for much of the summer and had considered Harvey Barnes and Crysencio Summerville, among others. Yet in the end, they took Alejandro Garnacho, a player Chelsea did not want who is now on loan at Villa.

Youngster George Hemmings was preferred to Garnacho in the opening day thrashing at Brighton and the Argentine did not come on until the 86th minute even though Villa were 4-0 down by half-time. With Ibrahim Mbaye, a long-term target, now through the door, Garnacho is competing for spots with Hemmings, Mbaye, John McGinn and Emi Buendia, who can all operate on the flanks.

Though there was tentative interest from Tottenham in Jackson, Daily Mail Sport was told in late July that if the Senegal forward left Chelsea, it would be for Villa. Likewise, when Villa had an Emi Martinez-shaped problem and Chelsea needed a goalkeeper, the next steps were no surprise.

All of this is perfectly within the rules and when clubs are constantly trying to manage UEFA’s often baffling rules, they will pull any legal lever they can. You scratch my back, I’ll scratch yours.

Who has the edge?

Looking at these deals with fresh eyes, you would assume that Chelsea were in the Champions League and Villa absent from Europe, not the other way around.

The Stamford Bridge club have taken a World Cup winning goalkeeper and one of the best English attackers from Villa. In return, they have sent them two players they no longer wanted.

Dig a little deeper, though. To follow the business plan imposed by UEFA, Villa needed a big sale and Rogers was by far their top asset. So he went for £117m – problem solved. When Villa signed Zion Suzuki, Martinez looked like he was going to Juventus. That move collapsed and suddenly Villa had three senior goalkeepers, including their highest earner.

Now Chelsea have taken away that burden, while landing a huge upgrade on the shaky Robert Sanchez into the bargain.

According to the Deloitte Money League, Chelsea’s revenue for 2025 was more than £100m greater than Villa’s, and they are highly efficient sellers. Chelsea’s buys may help them win the title.

Nicolas Jackson played under Unai Emery at Villarreal and the Villa boss knows he can hit the ground running

The reward for Villa is unlikely to be as great, especially regarding Garnacho, and it will soon become clear how much Emery really wanted the 22-year-old.

Last season, Villa took Harvey Elliott on loan from Liverpool only to decide they did not want him, and he was barely played all season so Villa did not have to sign him permanently. There is a similar obligation in Garnacho’s arrangement. Watch this space.

Yet Jackson is a different kettle of fish and may prove the ideal successor to Ollie Watkins. The 25-year-old started well at Chelsea but then-boss Enzo Maresca lost patience with his poor disciplinary record – eight yellow and two red cards in the 2024-25 season. He then struggled to make a significant impression on loan at Bayern Munich, despite scoring eight goals in only 12 league starts.

With Emery, though, it should be different. The pair first worked together at Villarreal and though Emery had left when Jackson really took off, scoring 10 goals in 11 games in 2023 before moving to Chelsea, the connection had been forged. Jackson trusts Emery and vice-versa. Emery likes players who fit into his plans immediately and Jackson should certainly do that.

The hand of Sawiris

Little happens at Aston Villa without the approval of Emery. He has been given free rein to hire the staff he likes and – regardless of the version the club like to push – he has been given a level of control over transfers that few managers have.

It is highly unlikely that Sawiris would allow anything that Emery had vetoed. Yet the Egyptian billionaire is becoming an ever more significant player in European football and this has been noticeable during the window. Daily Mail Sport first revealed on May 1 that Villa wanted Mbaye and the deal was undoubtedly helped by the personal rapport between Sawiris and Paris Saint-Germain chief Nasser Al-Khelaifi.

Alejandro Garnacho joined Villa from Chelsea, one of four trades between the clubs this summer along with Morgan Rogers, Martinez and Jackson

When Emery was hired in autumn 2022, former chief executive Christian Purslow namechecked Jorge Mendes’ agency, Gestifute, in his opening remarks. Mendes has a good relationship with Emery and had proposed AC Milan forward Rafael Leao to Villa, though the Portugal international ultimately chose the far higher salary on offer at Galatasaray.

Mendes is also believed to have brokered Mbaye’s move to Villa Park and last summer, he is thought to have been involved in trying to find a new club for Martinez – who has now ended up at Stamford Bridge. Not everyone in football is fond of Mendes but given his connections, it makes sense to keep him in your contacts list.

The coming months – indeed, the next 48 hours – will tell us which of these clubs will do better from their trading. Yet with UEFA creating an ever more complicated financial puzzle for clubs to solve, is it really any surprise if occasionally they help one another out?

Sports.title: Gary Neville accuses Liverpool of 'leaving Andoni Iraola short' with 'bizarre' recruitment: Pundit sends warning to Reds boss as he hits out at failure to sign full-backs and criticises decision to sell Cody Gakpo
Sports.content:
Gary Neville has accused Liverpool of leaving Andoni Iraola with an uncompetitive squad due to their 'bizarre' transfer dealings this summer.

The pundit is flabbergasted to see the Reds potentially selling Cody Gakpo to rivals Manchester City for £85million.

And he cannot believe they have failed to sign a full back and a holding midfielder - a shortcoming which will see them 'concede a lot,' according to Neville.

Liverpool have had to settle for two 2-2 draws against Newcastle and Nottingham Forest to start the season and look vulnerable whenever the opposition attack.

Neville said on his podcast: 'It's bizarre. The noise that Gakpo might leave - I know that Barcola might come in - but he looks like their best forward. I think he's a real danger.

'Someone like him can maybe not be appreciated at times. He's always involved and you should never underestimate a player [like him]. There's a lot of scruffy things he does but he always keeps coming back, he always wants the ball and he's always there. He does contribute with goals and with assists, maybe not at a massive level, but it's hard to replace lads like him.

Gary Neville has accused Liverpool of 'leaving Andoni Iraola short' despite their summer spend

He does not trust the defensive credentials of Milos Kerkez (above) and Jeremie Frimpong

'When your main opponents are looking to take him off you, I always think that is a bit of a worry and I don't think they can afford to lose him.

'But what's the most bizarre is that they haven't signed a full-back, left back and a right back. [Milos] Kerkez and [Jeremie] Frimpong look like the ideal wing-backs in a back five. It looks like a squad that could play a back three.

'If they're going to play a back four, and Kerkez and Frimpong are going to play full-back, and they're not going to sign a holding midfielder, Liverpool are going to concede a lot of goals.

'With the two goals against Forest, the right back is nowhere to be seen on the first one and on the second one, he lets the runner go from a throw-in when he should just mark him and go with him all the way. He's not got a natural instinct of how to defend.

'We used to criticise Trent Alexander-Arnold for his defensive work. To put this into context, TAA is a lot better defender than Frimpong, and he used to contribute 15-20 assists in a season. I don't think Frimpong will.

'Kerkez doesn't look like he's settled. At one point last season I thought he looked like an academy player playing at left-back for Liverpool and he's not - he's a very good player but they can't play with those two at full back and expect not to concede goals.

'I'm not sure what's going on there in respect of their recruitment. I don't think they have the numbers in defence. I think they're leaving Andoni Iraola well short. I know he looks like a gentleman and you see him in the interviews but if I was him I'd be demanding something in the next 48 hours because it will cost him.

'They will concede a lot of goals if those two play at full back in a normal traditional back four with that midfield.

He cannot comprehend the prospect of them selling Cody Gakpo to Manchester City for £85m

Neville says that Iraola should be 'demanding' more signings from Liverpool's hierarchy

'There's real excitement with the players they've got up top and if they added a defensive midfield player, and two good full backs, they'd have a really good chance.

'But they're being undermined by a lack of recruitment in those full back areas and in central midfield. They need to do something.'

Liverpool have at least addressed their shortage at centre-back, bringing in Jeremy Jacquet from Rennes for £60m and Ronald Araujo on loan from Barcelona.

Up top, Bradley Barcola is poised to sign from Paris Saint-Germain for £123m, and they have already added Victor Munoz, who scored his first goal against Forest, for £34m from Osasuna.

But the Reds have never truly replaced Fabinho in the No 6 role.

They do have Conor Bradley and Kostas Tsimikas as back-ups in the full-back areas, but they are not known for being overly defensive either.
