The CMC maintained that the host of a meeting may facilitate that meeting, but the leadership of a united opposition must emerge from an agreed process involving all participating parties.

“The CMC will not enter a fixed structure created without its participation. Unity cannot mean that independent political institutions are invited to join an arrangement whose leadership, authority, and operating framework have already been determined.”

CMC maintained that genuine opposition unity must be collectively discussed, developed, and owned.

Call for dialogue

It proposed that a proper starting point should be a preliminary dialogue among the major opposition political parties, meeting as equal and independent institutions.

It noted that such dialogue should establish a process through which the various opposition parties will develop a common assessment of Liberia’s present political, economic, governance, security, and democratic challenges, and clearly identify what has gone wrong in Liberia and agree upon what must never be allowed to happen again.

CMC stressed that such dialogue would also establish the principles, national priorities, and standards that will guide the collective opposition, prepare a clear contract with the Liberian people, setting out what the opposition will defend, what it will change, and what an opposition government will commit itself to delivering.

It emphasized that at the dialogue opposition political party leaders can agree upon a governing framework, decision-making procedures, conflict-resolution mechanisms, and the responsibilities of every participating institution and determine, through an open and mutually accepted process, how the leadership of the opposition collaboration will be derived.

“This process should operate at four interconnected levels. The political leaders should agree upon the broad vision and principles. The national chairpersons should coordinate the institutional process. The secretaries general should develop the operational arrangements. A technical team, comprising an equal number of qualified representatives from each major participating political party, should then draft the proposed framework for consideration, amendment, and final adoption.”

CMC further proposed that only after that framework has been discussed and adopted should any collective leadership, secretariat, coordinating authority, or other office be established.

Not genuine

The party says it cannot accept the invitation from the CDC in its present form as the proposed roundtable does not meet the requirements of an inclusive process intended to build genuine opposition collaboration.

It pointed out that its latest action is not a rejection of opposition unity, but a call for opposition unity to be built correctly, credibly, and sustainably.

The CMC pointed out that if the CDC and the other major opposition political parties agree to reconstitute the proposed meeting as a preliminary consultation among equals, without predetermined collective leadership, coordinating authority, or outcome, it (CMC) will be among the first to take its place at the table.

World.title: Liberia: LACC Marks 18th Anniversary, Pushes Prevention, Prosecution, and Recovery of Stolen Assets
World.content:
Monrovia — The Liberia Anti-Corruption Commission has celebrated its 18th anniversary with renewed calls for stronger prevention of corruption, institutional collaboration, prosecution, and recovery of public resources lost through corruption.

By Francis G. Boayue

The anniversary celebration held over the weekend in Monrovia brought together current and former LACC officials, government representatives, civil society actors, media practitioners, and other stakeholders involved in Liberia’s anti-corruption efforts.

The LACC was established on August 28, 2008, following post-war governance reforms and recommendations for the creation of an independent institution to lead Liberia’s fight against corruption.

Speaking during the ceremony, LACC Executive Chairperson Cllr. Alexandra K. Zoe, who delivered a presentation titled “18 Years of the LACC — A Journey in Numbers,” said the Commission’s progress over the past 18 years has been marked by institutional growth, legal reforms, and increased public awareness.

She stressed, however, that the fight against corruption cannot be won by the Commission alone.

“This is not an easy fight, and it’s not something that LACC can do alone,” Zoe said, urging citizens to report corruption and help create awareness in communities beyond the Commission’s reach.

“Your role is to report. Your role is to create additional awareness in areas that we cannot reach,” she added.

Zoe said the Commission’s 2022 amended and restated Act represents a major milestone, as it granted the LACC direct prosecutorial powers.

Previously, the Commission was required to forward investigative reports to the Ministry of Justice for prosecution, with the Ministry given 90 days to act on cases. According to Zoe, the arrangement contributed to delays and sometimes weakened the prospects of successful prosecution.

She said the Commission is now exercising its prosecutorial authority but needs a specialized court to efficiently adjudicate corruption cases.

Zoe welcomed ongoing efforts toward the establishment of a specialized anti-corruption court, saying it would facilitate speedy trials and ultimately strengthen efforts to recover stolen public assets.

“When this court is established, what it does is that it will create a speedy trial, and then it should ultimately lead to recovery,” she said.

She said the Commission’s focus must increasingly shift toward recovering public resources in existing cases while strengthening prevention to stop new cases of corruption.

Zoe also called for increased budgetary support, stressing that the Commission remains understaffed and under-resourced relative to the scale of Liberia’s corruption challenges.

She said the LACC has grown from a small institution with a skeleton staff to its current structure but still lacks sufficient personnel, particularly prosecutors, to effectively execute its mandate.

The Executive Chairperson said increased funding is critical to implementing the Commission’s 2026–2030 Strategic Plan, which focuses on prevention, enforcement, partnerships, and institutional strengthening.

She also called for greater institutional independence and sustained support from government and development partners.

Delivering the keynote address, Minister of State for Presidential Affairs Hon. Samuel A. Stevquoah said Liberia’s next phase of the anti-corruption fight must prioritize prevention, institutional cooperation, and consequences.

“We cannot investigate our way out of corruption,” Stevquoah said, warning that investigations often come after public resources have already been lost.

He called for stronger procurement systems, internal controls, audits, asset declaration and verification, digital financial systems, and other mechanisms designed to make corruption more difficult to commit.

The Minister also urged closer collaboration among integrity institutions, including the General Auditing Commission, Internal Audit Agency, Ministry of Justice, Financial Intelligence Agency, Public Procurement and Concessions Commission, and Liberia Revenue Authority.

“Too often in government we see institutions that operate in silos,” he said, calling for improved information sharing and more efficient movement of cases from audit and investigation through prosecution and adjudication.

Stevquoah said accountability must be both firm and fair, with due process respected.

“At 18, the LACC is no longer a young institution,” he said. “You’ve matured.”

He urged the Commission to be “fearless” while remaining fair, independent, collaborative, and aggressive in protecting public resources while respecting due process.

For his part, former LACC Executive Chairperson Cllr. James N. Verdier reflected on the Commission’s early struggles, urging current officials to remain resilient in the face of political pressure, criticism, and public skepticism.

Verdier, who served as Executive Chairperson from 2013 to 2019, clarified that Cllr. Frances Johnson-Morris was the Commission’s first chairperson.

He recalled that during his tenure, the LACC faced significant limitations under the law, particularly regarding prosecution and enforcement.

He said the Commission pushed the boundaries of its existing legal authority, including making arrests in corruption investigations, while advocating for stronger legislation.

Verdier also emphasized the importance of professional training for investigators and greater investment in forensic investigative capabilities.

He further stressed that asset declaration must be accompanied by verification.

“The crux of the asset declaration is the verification,” Verdier said, calling for adequate resources to determine whether assets declared by public officials are accurate.

In remarks, the National Civil Society Council of Liberia President Lawrence Yealue said the fight against corruption must begin in homes and communities by teaching children honesty, integrity, and accountability.

“The fight against corruption starts here in our homes,” Yealue said.

He argued that prevention should receive greater attention than prosecution, while urging the media to highlight honest public servants instead of giving excessive attention to individuals accused of corruption.

“There are more good people in this country than bad people,” Yealue said, calling for greater recognition of public servants who demonstrate integrity.

As the LACC enters its 19th year, its leadership says the institution’s next chapter will focus on strengthening prevention, enforcement, prosecution, and recovery while rebuilding public confidence.

“We don’t need to be making excuses anymore. The public has our attention. Now is the time to build their trust,” Zoe said.

World.title: CAF Invites Cllr. Kunkunyon Wleh Teh to Addis Ababa Governance Meeting
World.content:
MONROVIA — The Confederation of African Football (CAF) has formally invited Liberian legal practitioner Cllr. Kunkunyon Wleh Teh to participate in a high-level governance meeting scheduled for September in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia a development that could further elevate Liberia’s representation in continental football administration.

By Christopher C. Walker | [email protected]

According to an official invitation letter dated August 25, 2026, CAF has summoned members of its Governance Committee to an in-person session at the Ethiopian Skylight Hotel in Addis Ababa from September 15 to 19, 2026.

The correspondence, signed by CAF Acting General Secretary Samson Adamu, states that the meeting is being convened to allow the Governance Committee to deliberate on critical governance matters within its statutory mandate and formulate recommendations for the CAF Executive Committee.

Cllr. Teh is slated to contribute to the proceedings as part of his ongoing engagement with CAF’s governance framework.

The invitation comes at a pivotal time when institutional accountability, administrative compliance, and structural integrity have taken center stage across African football.

Governance Agenda

CAF’s letter clarifies that the Addis Ababa gathering is a statutory session of the continental body’s Governance Committee rather than a ceremonial event.

The committee’s operations are anchored in Article 44 of the CAF Statutes, which delineates its mandate and oversight responsibilities. According to CAF, committee members will evaluate pressingly relevant governance issues and draft policy recommendations aimed at guiding the Executive Committee’s broader administrative decisions.

The continental body requested that all invited members confirm their availability promptly to facilitate travel and logisitical arrangements.

Cllr. Teh’s involvement positions him among a select group of legal minds and sports administrators shaping the regulatory direction of the African game.

Relevance to Liberian Football

The invitation arrives amidst heightened scrutiny of local football administration, particularly following recent controversies involving the Liberia Football Association (LFA) and the nation’s non-participation in continental club tournaments.

An LFA investigative panel was recently constituted to examine the circumstances surrounding Liberia’s failure to feature in the 2026/27 CAF Men’s Interclub Competitions—a lapse that sparked public outcry and raised concerns over administrative efficiency, internal communication, and regulatory compliance within the domestic governing body.

In light of these local challenges, Liberia’s involvement in continental governance forums carries added weight. While CAF’s invitation letter does not tie the Addis Ababa meeting to any specific ongoing investigation or disciplinary action involving the LFA, Cllr. Teh’s attendance highlights the importance of aligning local administrative systems with broader continental standards.

Continental Engagement

For Cllr. Teh, the multi-day session provides another platform to interface directly with CAF leadership and legal experts.

As African football continues to prioritize transparency, institutional independence, and ethical governance, the outcomes of the September meeting are expected to play a role in refining how member associations and continental structures are monitored.

Cllr. Teh is expected to depart for Ethiopia prior to the September 15 opening session.

World.title: We Must Not Forget The Victims Of Liberia’s Civil War
World.content:
Liberia’s fourteen years of civil conflict ended long ago, but many of its victims are still suffering. Some live with bullets and fragments in their bodies, lost limbs, impaired vision, chronic pain and emotional trauma. Others remain in poverty because the war destroyed their homes, farms, businesses and families. Many feel abandoned and forgotten by the country for whose conflict they paid such a terrible price.

By Tiawan Saye Gongloe

At the end of the war, former fighters received disarmament and demobilization packages, including money, vocational training and other forms of assistance to help them return to civilian life. That support was necessary for peace. But it created a painful imbalance: those who carried the guns received organized assistance, while many of the people injured, widowed, displaced and impoverished by the war received little or nothing. Liberia must correct this historic injustice.

I therefore propose the creation of a National War Victims Relief Fund for an initial period of five years. Every unemployed adult Liberian who is able to contribute should pay L$100 per year. Every employed Liberian should contribute US$1 per year, and Liberians living abroad should also be encouraged to contribute at least US$1 annually. The Government should match these contributions at a ratio of US$5 for every US$1 contributed under the national scheme.

The fund should be used to provide medical treatment, medication, prosthetic devices and modest welfare support to severely disabled victims. It should also provide interest-free microloans to victims who can engage in farming, trading or small businesses. The goal should be to reduce suffering, restore independence and give victims renewed hope in a caring Liberia.

This fund must be completely separate from the establishment of the War and Economic Crimes Court. The court concerns accountability for crimes committed during the conflict. The relief fund concerns care and responsibility for people who are suffering today. A wounded victim who needs medicine should not have to wait for a prosecution, and a widow living in poverty should not have to wait for the creation of a court before receiving assistance. Liberia can pursue justice and care for victims at the same time.

The fund must also be transparent and protected from political interference. A credible national registry of qualified victims should be established, and the General Auditing Commission should audit the fund annually. Most importantly, administrative expenses should not be deducted from the victims’ money. Salaries, offices and other operating costs should come from a separate appropriation in the national budget.

Someone may ask, “Why now?” The answer is simple: it is better late than never. The passage of time does not erase the suffering of those who still carry the physical, emotional and economic scars of the war. Delay is not a reason for continued neglect; it is a reason to act now.

This is more than a financial proposal. It is a national statement that Liberia remembers its victims, cares about their suffering and accepts responsibility for helping them rebuild their lives.

Such collective care can help heal old wounds, restore hope and make victims feel that their country has not abandoned them.

The fighters were assisted because Liberia needed peace. The victims must now be assisted because justice, compassion and national responsibility demand it.

We must not and cannot forget the victims of Liberia’s civil conflict.

World.title: Daka makes quiet Bundesliga debut
World.content:
Chipolopolo and Hamburg striker Patson Daka made a low-key Bundesliga debut on Saturday as his new side fell 2-0 to Borussia Dortmund on the opening weekend of the new season.

It was Daka’s first league appearance in Germany, just over a month after switching from England.

The Zambian international started up front and played 67 minutes before being replaced by Nigerian Terem Moffi.

Daka’s biggest moment came in the second half when he struck the outside of the post following good link-up play from Louis Lemke.

According to match statistics from BBC Sport, the former Leicester man registered three shots on the day in front of a crowd of 81,365 fans.

Dortmund took control early. Serhou Guirassy and Giannis Konstantelias scored to give BVB a 2-0 win and three points to start their Bundesliga campaign.

Daka joins Hamburg after five years at Leicester City, a spell that saw the club suffer two relegations from the Premier League to League One.

Before England, he starred in Austria with Red Bull Salzburg.

Hamburg will look to bounce back when they host Mainz in their next Bundesliga fixture.

Internationally, Daka is expected to lead the Chipolopolo frontline in next month’s back-to-back Africa Cup qualifiers against Algeria and Togo.

World.title: Mundubile, Makebi Zulu, Findlay Transferred to Mukobeko on Treason Charges
World.content:
Opposition leader Brian Mundubile, his running mate Makebi Zulu and businessman Harry Findlay were flown under armed guard to Mukobeko Maximum Security Facility in Kabwe on Saturday, hours after being charged with treason alongside sixteen others.

The trio were airlifted aboard a Zambia Police Service helicopter between 05:00 and 06:00 hours and received at the facility by prison officials, according to their lawyer, Milner Katolo.

Police say the three conspired to overthrow the government by unlawful means between 1 and 16 August in Lusaka, an offence charged under Section 43 of the Penal Code, Chapter 87 of the Laws of Zambia.

Zambia Police Service spokesperson Godfrey Chilabi confirmed the charges were formalised on Saturday, putting the total number of accused at 18.

A day after the election results were announced, security personnel raided a property in Lusaka’s Kabulonga area linked to Mundubile. Several suspects were nabbed at the scene.

Police say firearms, ammunition and tactical gear, allegedly connected to an armed insurrection plot, were recovered from the property.

Following the raid, Mundubile and Zulu took refuge inside a United Nations building in Lusaka. The UN, working alongside church mother bodies, later handed the pair to their lawyers.

The two politicians were subsequently picked up by police for questioning before being formally charged.

Treason is a non-bailable offence in Zambia. The case will be heard exclusively by the High Court, meaning neither man can apply for bail at a lower court while the matter proceeds.

Mundubile contested the 13 August presidential election as candidate for the National Reconciliation Party for Unity and Progress. He secured 38 percent of the vote against President Hakainde Hichilema’s 60 percent, according to results declared by the Electoral Commission of Zambia.

Others jointly charged with Mundubile and Zulu include Trevor Mwamba, lawyer George Chisanga, Patrick Mwansa and Jackson Mutyoka.

Also facing charges are Brazil Soko, Bernard Chewe, Simon Phiri, Richard Banda, Francis Mulenga, Emmanuel Mulenga and Darius Mwila.

Katolo said the accused will appear in court once committal proceedings have concluded, adding that investigations remain ongoing.

Mukobeko Maximum Security Facility has been cordoned off by combined teams of military and police personnel, with access to the area restricted.

Security has also been heightened in Kabwe town, according to police.

The developments come as Zambia braces for tomorrow’s presidential inauguration, with the country’s security wings on heightened alert around the National Heroes Stadium in Lusaka.

The case has already drawn sharply divided reaction from political and civic figures. Tonse Alliance secretary general Dr Chris Zumani Zimba has called for dialogue and a political ceasefire, citing the human cost of the post-election crisis, including reported detentions and the death of former minister Mutotwe Kafwaya.

By contrast, UPND campaign chairman for Southern Province John Chidyaka has urged Zambians to move past politicking and focus on national development, describing the inauguration as a unifying moment for the country.

Governance watchdogs, including the Foundation for Democratic Process, have separately urged losing candidates pursuing election petitions to ensure they have sufficient evidence before approaching the courts.

The National Reconciliation Party for Unity and Progress has not yet issued a formal response to the treason charges against its leadership.

The Mukobeko transfer follows a period of heightened uncertainty since results were declared, during which opposition figures disputed the outcome and several parliamentary petitions were filed challenging results in individual constituencies.

Police say investigations into the alleged conspiracy remain active, with further details expected to be released in due course.

World.title: Govt. disburses K1.7 billion for Livingstone-Sesheke road works
World.content:
Government has released over K1.7 billion for the reconstruction of the Livingstone- Sesheke road which has been in dilapidated state.

This came to light during a public disclosure meeting held in Mwandi for the Environmental and Social Impact Assessment of the Livingstone-Sesheke road project.

Speaking during a public disclosure meeting in Mwandi, Bari Zambia Consultants, Environmental and Social Advisor, Lackson Chilongo revealed that the road is undergoing rapid designing and planning for six months to pave way for the construction works to commence before the onset of the rainy season.

Mr Chilongo said the entire project will be implemented in a period of 30 months.

He added that the Road Development Agency (RDA), will work closely with the contracted company Sinohydro Corporation Limited in a joint venture with Nchifar Enterprises Limited.

Mr Chilongo explained that the project is divided into Lot 1 and Lot 2, saying Lot 1 is the first 65 kilometers from Livingstone to Kazungula heading to 165 kilometers of Simungoma to Sesheke while Lot 2 is the 100 kilometers stretch from Kazungula to Simungoma of Mwandi district which is the most affected area.

He stated that Lot 1 has been allocated 15 kilometers township roads, 10 kilometers for Livingstone and five kilometers in Sesheke.

Mr Chilongo added that Lot 2 will receive 10 kilometers shared between Kazungula and Mwandi districts with five kilometers each of township roads.

He noted that the project will provide 400 jobs and local people will be prioritised.

And Mwandi District Commissioner, Sikuka Mwitumwa has expressed delight over the development and thanked government through President Hakainde Hichilema for walking the talk on the road project.

“God has remembered us because Mwandi district is the most affected by the bad road, the road is worse when entering and leaving Mwandi district,” she said.

Ms Mwitumwa further said it is encouraging that Lot 2 will be worked on first, to show that government cares for the people of Mwandi district.

She noted that once the road is complete, Mwandi residents will save on traveling time, open the area to capital projects, improve the market and reduce tear and wear on vehicles.

Mrs Mwitumwa stated that the Livingstone-Sesheke road, is an international road and working on it to a bituminous standard will improve international trade.

She has since called on the District Development Coordinating Committee (DDCC), to cooperate with all stakeholders during the 30 months lifecycle of the project.

Meanwhile, Barotse Royal Establishment, Mwandi Kuta Induna, Lawrence Sinyani who is Induna Omei, said the kuta has already allocated land to the construction company where they will be camping.

Induna Omei disclosed that the Kuta will also provide some quarry from Sesheke to the road project and also assured to render support to the project with anything needed that is within their control.

The traditional leadership has welcomed the development and thanked government saying that once completed, the road will open Mwandi to more development.

World.title: Milenge maintains clean record in livestock disease control
World.content:
Milenge District Livestock and Fisheries Officer, Chongo Kafula, says the district has maintained a clean record this year, with zero cases of Contagious Bovine Pleuropneumonia (CBPP) and other major livestock diseases.

‎Mr Kafula has attributed the district’ success as being tied to its location within Luapula Province, which is officially designated as a livestock disease-free zone.

‎

He stated that the area has not recorded significant outbreaks of tick-borne diseases or other livestock conditions so far this year.

‎

‎“Those major diseases I have mentioned are not in Luapula, so even in Milenge, they are not there,” he disclosed.

‎Mr Kafula however, explained that livestock vaccination exercises could still be conducted once relevant authorities consider it necessary especially, as a proactive measure to protect the province’s disease-free status, particularly in light of animal movements from other regions.

‎

‎He cited when the district had previously conducted vaccinations against Lumpy Skin Disease in 2023 and 2025, with the most recent exercise covering over 35 cattle.

‎

‎”It is for this reason that collectively maintaining robust surveillance and appropriate veterinary interventions remains critical to safeguarding the province’s prized disease-free status,” he said.

‎

He has since urged local livestock farmers to remain vigilant and report any suspected disease cases promptly to allow for timely intervention.

World.title: Government reaffirms support to farmers
World.content:
Government has reaffirmed its commitment to supporting small-scale farmers as agriculture remains critical to rural development, food security and economic empowerment.

Ministry of Local Government and Rural Development Permanent Secretary, Gabriel Pollen, says the government attaches great importance to the agriculture sector because of its contribution to improving livelihoods and driving development in rural communities.

Dr Pollen was speaking when he officiated at this year’s Chibwela Kumushi traditional ceremony of the Soli people of Bunda Bunda Chiefdom in Rufunsa District.

He said the government, through the Ministry of Agriculture, remains committed to supporting small-scale farmers through the Farmer Input Support Programme (FISP).

“Continued investment in agriculture is important in enabling farmers to increase production, improve household incomes and contribute to national food security,” he said.

Dr Pollen said continued investment in agriculture is important in enabling farmers to increase production, improve household incomes and contribute to national food security.

Meanwhile, Chief Bunda Bunda Chimapepe, the second, congratulated President Hakainde Hichilema on his re-election.

In a speech read on his behalf by his representative, Judge Edward Musona, Chief Bunda Bunda said the re-election provides an opportunity for the government to continue implementing development and strengthening democracy.

“The re-election of President Hakainde Hichilema provides an opportunity for the government to continue implementing its development agenda and strengthening democracy,” said Chief Bunda Bunda.

He also stressed the importance of preserving traditional ceremonies as a way of passing cultural values and traditions from one generation to another.

And Lusaka Province Permanent Secretary, Joe Kalusa commended the people of Rufunsa for re-electing President Hichilema for continued development.

Mr Kalusa said the re-election of President Hichilema attests to how people are appreciating his vision in taking development to all parts of the country.

“You have re-elected President Hichilema because you have seen what his government has done in the five years in power and more is yet to come,”said Mr Kalusa.

He further said traditional ceremonies play an important role in preserving Zambia’s diverse cultural heritage.

Mr Kalusa said such gatherings provide communities with an opportunity to celebrate their traditions while promoting unity and social cohesion.

Rufunsa District Commissioner, Richard Mabena also reaffirmed the government’s commitment to working with traditional leaders and communities to promote development while preserving cultural heritage.

The ceremony, which was held under the theme “Promoting Cultural Heritage,” brought together traditional leaders, government officials, community members and other dignitaries to celebrate the farming season and the community’s harvest.

World.title: Boko toasts President Hichilema on re-election
World.content:
Botswana President Duma Boko, has congratulated President Hakainde Hichilema on his re-election, describing the milestone as an important moment for the people of Zambia.

In a congratulatory message, President Boko said Botswana joins the people of Zambia in celebrating President Hichilema’s re-election and expressed confidence that the two countries will continue to strengthen their long standing bilateral relations.

“Zambia and Botswana share deep historical ties, common values and a strong commitment to peace, democracy and regional integration,” President Boko said.

World.title: Zambia prepares for President Hichilema’ second-term inauguration
World.content:
Zambia is preparing for the inauguration of President Hakainde Hichilema on 1st September 2026, marking the beginning of his second five-year term.

Ministry of Information and Media Director Spokesperson, Henry Kapata, says the inauguration comes as the country reflects on a first term that saw Zambia tackle debt restructuring, high inflation, energy shortages and weak investor confidence, while laying the foundation for the next phase of economic growth.

Mr Kapata has told the media business news that inflation has fallen from 24.6 percent in December 2021 to 6.2 percent in August 2026, while international reserves have risen to around US$6.5 billion.

He said the second term comes with clearly defined ambitions under the 10-10-5-3-3-1-1 development framework:

Mr Kapata explained that the development framework includes 10,000MW electricity generation capacity, 10 million tonnes of maize production, 5 million annual international tourist arrivals, 3 million tonnes of copper production, 3 million tonnes of soybean production, and 3 million tonnes of wheat production as well as US$1 billion of annual beef export revenue.

Mr Kapata further said the targets are aimed at expanding production, attracting investment, creating jobs, strengthening exports and improving household incomes.

“As preparations continue ahead of Tuesday’s ceremony, we look at the journey so far, the economic foundation Zambia enters the second term with and what these targets mean for the country’s next five years. The mandate has been renewed. The targets are defined. The next chapter is delivery,” he said.

World.title: Technology key in promoting tourism sector-Kangwa
World.content:
Secretary to the Cabinet, Patrick Kangwa, says embracing technology and innovation can help Zambia promote its tourism sector by finding new and engaging ways of telling the country’s story.

Mr Kangwa says the integration of technology into tourism can improve visitor experiences, showcase Zambia’s cultural heritage and contribute to job creation and economic development.

Mr Kangwa said this in Lusaka last night during the 2026 Thousands of Miles on the Silk Road-Colours of Africa Transnational Drone Light Show, which celebrated Zambia-China relations through culture, technology and creativity.

“Technology can become a powerful tool for tourism storytelling,” he said.

Mr Kangwa said Zambia and China have maintained strong relations for over 60 years, with the partnership extending to sectors such as trade, investment, infrastructure, tourism, culture and people-to-people exchanges.

Mr Kangwa said the Tanzania-Zambia Railway Authority remains an important symbol of the longstanding friendship between Zambia and China and was among the shared milestones highlighted during the drone display.

He said the Brand Zambia Initiative, launched in March this year under the tagline “Zambia Moves You,” provides a platform for showcasing the country’s tourism potential, cultural heritage, peace and investment opportunities.

“We must use innovation to market Zambia beyond our borders,” he said.

Mr Kangwa said Government is targeting more than 2.5 million international tourist arrivals and over US$1 billion in tourism earnings by the end of 2026.

He stated that achieving the target will require Zambia to develop quality tourism products and market the country more deliberately, creatively and competitively.

And Ministry of Tourism Permanent Secretary, Evans Muhanga said the drone light show demonstrated the potential of combining technology and creativity with tourism and cultural promotion.

Mr Muhanga said Zambia has a wide range of natural and cultural tourism assets which can be promoted through innovative platforms to attract both local and international visitors.

“Innovation can enrich the visitor experience,” Mr. Muhanga said.

He said the event also provided an opportunity to celebrate the longstanding friendship between Zambia and China while highlighting their shared culture, heritage and history through modern technology.

Mr Muhanga said the Ministry of Tourism will continue collaborating with various stakeholders to strengthen Zambia’s position as a competitive tourism and events destination.

He added that the Ministry of Tourism also contributed about K150,000 towards the event, to ensure that the drone light show could be recorded and broadcast on Zambia National Broadcasting Corporation (ZNBC).

Meanwhile, Chinese Ambassador to Zambia, Han Jing, says China and Zambia will continue to deepen their longstanding all-weather friendship through practical cooperation in various sectors.

Mr Han said the drone light show held in Lusaka is another highlight of the celebrations and demonstrates how technology can be used to promote cultural understanding and strengthen ties between the two countries.

He said technology and innovation should ultimately improve people’s livelihoods, citing the use of drones in agriculture monitoring, emergency disaster response, delivery of medical supplies to remote communities and ecological conservation.

Mr Han said China remains committed to working with Zambia in promoting people-centred development through practical cooperation, technology and stronger people-to-people relations.

The event was supported by Shaanxi Radio and Television Media Convergence Group Company Limited, Shenzhen High Great Technology Company Limited, the Embassy of the People’s Republic of China in Zambia and the Zambia Chinese Association, among other cooperating partners.

World.title: Africa: All of Africa Today - August 31, 2026
World.content:
Russia Says It Helped Foil Niger Coup

Russia has said that its African Corps forces helped Nigerien troops repel an attempted coup in the capital, Niamey, after explosions and gunfire were reported near a key military airbase and the presidential palace. Nigerien authorities later said the rebellion had been contained. Russia said the situation was under the control of President Abdourahmane Tiani's government. The Alliance of Sahel States, comprising Niger, Mali and Burkina Faso, condemned the attempted takeover as an effort to destabilise the country. The incident highlights continued security challenges in Niger, where jihadist violence persists despite the military government's closer ties with Russia and its break from Western partners.

Zambian Opposition Leader Brian Mundubile Charged With Treason



Zambian opposition leader Brian Mundubile has been charged with treason alongside 17 others, including his running mate Makebi Zulu. This follows growing political tensions after the country's presidential election. Mundubile, who disputed President Hakainde Hichilema's victory, went into hiding after security forces raided a property linked to him in Lusaka. The security forces also killed a former cabinet minister and arrested several other politicians. The government said it recovered weapons during the operation. Mundubile's party denied allegations that it was planning an armed insurgency. Mundubile won 38% of the vote against Hichilema's 60%. The president is due to be sworn in for a second term on September 1.

Turkish and Somali Forces Free Hijacked Ship Off Somalia Coast

Turkish and Somali forces have freed a Cameroon-flagged vessel hijacked off Somalia after a 10-day operation that left 14 suspected pirates dead. Somalia's Defence Ministry said four boats used by the pirates were destroyed and that sustained military pressure forced the remaining attackers to abandon the vessel, which has since resumed its journey. At least eight crew members were reportedly aboard the MV LATUF, including one Turkish national. Authorities did not provide details about casualties or their condition. The operation comes as piracy resurges along Somalia's coast, with at least 15 attacks recorded this year. These attacks are the highest since 2013. The resurgence of piracy in the Horn of Africa is adding to mounting challenges for international shipping in the Middle East, where vessels are already navigating around the contested Strait of Hormuz and seeking to avoid Houthi attacks in the Red Sea.

Amnesty Urges Kenya to Act on Enforced Disappearances

Amnesty International Kenya has called on the government to move beyond promises and take concrete action to end enforced disappearances, establish the whereabouts of missing people and hold those responsible accountable. The organisation welcomed President William Ruto's recent statement that no Kenyan should lose their life, liberty or dignity for criticising the government or participating in peaceful protests, but said his words must now be matched by action. Amnesty cited 19 enforced disappearances and 69 police killings recorded so far in 2026. They also pointed to 35 verified cases included in a recent reparations framework. It urged independent investigations, accountability and reparations for victims and families, as well as stronger protections for journalists, human rights defenders and protesters ahead of the 2027 elections.

Zimbabwe Declares State of Disaster After Highway Crash

Zimbabwe has declared a State of Disaster following a devastating road crash on the Harare-Masvingo highway that killed 27 people and left seven others critically injured. A haulage truck carrying mining equipment from South Africa and a commuter minibus carrying members of the African Apostolic (Mwazha) Church were involved in an accident near Honeyspruit Bridge in Chikomba District. The vehicles collided head-on and caught fire, with several passengers trapped inside the minibus. Twenty-four people died at the scene and three others later succumbed to their injuries at Chivhu General Hospital, while the truck driver survived and was taken to Harare for treatment. The disaster declaration will allow the government to mobilise additional resources and coordinate assistance for survivors and bereaved families.

Close 

Guinea-Bissau Voters Head to Polls on Expanded Presidential Powers

Voters in military-run Guinea-Bissau are set to vote in a referendum on a proposed new constitution that would significantly strengthen presidential powers ahead of general elections scheduled for December. The reforms would replace the parliamentary system with a presidential one, allowing the head of state to appoint and dismiss the prime minister and government and dissolve parliament. The junta says the changes are necessary to stabilise the country's institutions before civilian rule is restored, but the opposition has urged voters to boycott the referendum, citing restrictions on public freedoms. The vote comes less than a year after the military seized power following a presidential election, adding to Guinea-Bissau's long history of coups and political instability.

World.title: South Africa: SASSA Beneficiaries Face Black Card Deadline - South African News Briefs - August 31, 2026
World.content:
D-Day for 70,000 SASSA Beneficiaries to Get Black Cards

Nearly 70,000 South African Social Security Agency (SASSA) beneficiaries have yet to collect their new Postbank black cards as the deadline to replace the old gold cards ends, reports EWN. SASSA said the gold cards are no longer operational, but beneficiaries who miss the deadline can still collect their black cards at designated sites. They can find their nearest collection point by dialling 120355#, with only an ID required and no further registration needed.

Man Arrested in R635m Tembisa Hospital Tender Probe

A 37-year-old man is set to appear in the Specialised Commercial Crimes Court facing fraud, corruption and money laundering charges linked to an alleged R635 million Tembisa Hospital tender fraud case, reports SABC News. The Hawks arrested him at OR Tambo International Airport after he returned from overseas. Investigators allege hospital officials colluded with service providers and manipulated the procurement system by keeping transactions below R500,000 to avoid formal tender processes.

Call for Safer School Kitchens

A public health expert has called for more environmental health officers to oversee school kitchens, reports EWN. This comes after Parliament heard that only 18% of nearly 9,000 kitchens surveyed in six provinces had the required Certificate of Acceptability. Food safety specialist Asanda Getyeza-Ntswam urged stricter enforcement of municipal regulations and better training for food handlers. She warned that poor hygiene and inadequate food storage could put children's health at risk.

World.title: Mozambique: Military Personnel Must Remain Ready to Face Growing Sophisticated Threats
World.content:
Maputo — Mozambican President and Commander-in-Chief of the Defense and Security Forces (FDS), Daniel Chapo, has encouraged the country's military personnel to remain ready to respond to growing and increasingly sophisticated threats to national security.

Speaking at the ceremony marking the 31st Commando Course at the Special Forces Training School in Nacala, in the northern province of Nampula, Chapo argued that military readiness can no longer rely solely on weaponry and troop numbers.

"New conflict scenarios demand a combination of modern equipment, specialized training, intelligence, logistics, secure communications, decision-making capabilities, and mastery of new technologies. Modernizing the armed forces does not mean merely acquiring equipment, but also training men and women with the necessary capacity to operate that equipment", he said.

The President highlighted the changing nature of contemporary conflicts, which are increasingly characterized by the use of drones, surveillance systems, artificial intelligence, secure communications, and other technological tools.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

In this context, he deemed it essential that Commandos be prepared to operate in environments characterized by difficult, unpredictable, and highly complex situations. "Training must continue to be based on a rigorous selection and preparation process involving discipline, physical endurance, psychological readiness, and the acquisition of technical skills for field operations."

Addressing the finalists, Chapo emphasized that the position of Commander represents increased responsibilities and demands conduct based on values such as discipline, courage, readiness, loyalty, and commitment to the homeland.

"Therefore, act with integrity, firmness, and toughness when defending Mozambique. And this is non-negotiable. The homeland is priceless, and the defense of the homeland cannot be delegated," he stated.

The Head of State also advocated for leveraging the experience accumulated by Mozambican forces in combating terrorism in Cabo Delgado, considering it an important asset for improving the preparedness and operational capacity of the FDS.

"The defense of the homeland requires not only men with weapons in their hands, but also technology, logistics, doctrine, intelligence, information, leadership, and decision-making capacity in difficult moments," he declared.

According to Chapo, "the security situation in Cabo Delgado is currently showing improvements compared to previous periods. However, there is no room for complacency or relaxation. Always be on combat alert. Don't let routine replace readiness."

World.title: Africa: Is This The Bandage For Africa's Rising Medical Fabrics Demand?
World.content:
Local cotton manufacturing moves into surgical textiles as Africa seeks import alternatives and channels more fibre into homegrown factories.

African manufacturers are increasingly turning locally grown cotton into high-value medical textiles, offering a domestic alternative to raw exports and expensive imports.

The shift is still small compared with the size of the continent's cotton industry. But it comes as countries across the region are under pressure to produce more of the health products they consume.

As demand picks up, it has drawn entrepreneurs along the continent's cotton value chain who want an early foothold in a market poised for strong growth in the next four years.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Market research firm Mordor Intelligence forecasts the Africa textile market to reach $49.41 billion by 2030, up from $39.21 billion in 2025.

Tellingly, "medical and healthcare textiles are the fastest growing segment, projected at 5.71% CAGR through 2030", the firm said, pointing to rising demand for products used in hospitals and operating theatres.

"Nigeria, Kenya, and Ethiopia are building hospitals under public-private frameworks that standardise demand for surgical drapes, fluid-repellent gowns, and certified wound dressings." Mordor Intelligence attributes this growth to Covid-era reforms which made bulk buying of protective wear more routine.

This, it says, has encouraged IFC-backed factories in Ghana and Kenya to add clean-room production lines built to meet ISO 13485, the global standard for medical-grade production.

A move toward local sourcing of medical textiles could give manufacturers a steadier market than fashion, where producers often depend on foreign buyers and shifting orders.

For cotton-producing countries, the potential is massive because much of the raw material needed for these products is already grown locally.

In Ethiopia, Adama Development has already moved beyond cotton spinning. The company now operates a medical textile business, Nazmed Medical Textiles, alongside its cotton and textile operations.

A textile industry professional working for the company describes Nazmed as part of Adama Development's medical textile operations.

The development reflects a broader change in the way African manufacturers are looking at cotton for new opportunities to cash in from the crop. For decades, much of the continent's cotton has left in relatively unprocessed form.

UN Trade and Development estimates that 70% of Africa's cotton exports are primary intermediate products such as cotton fibre. Only 12% are yarn and 18% are cotton fabrics.

The OECD-FAO Agricultural Outlook projects that Africa will export nearly 80% of its cotton production by 2035, although the textile and apparel industries are expanding in countries like Ethiopia and Benin.

But the uptake of medical textiles could see the continent convert more of its cotton into finished healthcare products as fresh focus and investment flow into manufacturing.

New ventures are adding capacity further along the chain. In Zambia, a China-Zambia joint venture began test runs at Mulungushi Textiles in Kabwe in January 2026 after new machinery was installed.

The $140 million rehabilitation aims to revive textile production and create hundreds of direct jobs, while also supporting cotton outgrowers.

Everness Nankala, a principal public relations officer at Zambia’s Ministry of Commerce, Trade and Industry, said the project was “a testament to the government’s commitment to promoting industrial growth and creating employment opportunities for Zambians.” The plant is also expected to “reduce reliance on imports, and promote inclusive development,” she said.

In Zambia, another entrepreneur is already turning cotton into a medical product. Carrivorious Simasinti began producing surgical cotton wool after seeing his country export raw cotton and then import absorbent cotton products.

Simasinti founded Premier Multipurpose Cooperative Society in 2016. His factory processes cotton lint into absorbent and surgical cotton wool for medical and sanitary use.

In 2021, when UNCTAD profiled the business, the factory was producing about 7,200 kg of surgical cotton wool a month. About 70% was sold within Zambia and the remaining 30% exported to neighbouring countries.

“Demand for the product is high,” Simasinti told UN Trade and Development.

The company had also developed an outgrower scheme involving more than 100 farmers. Together, they had covered 250 hectares and were expected to produce 150 tonnes of seed cotton. But shortages of raw cotton, limited machinery and transport problems restricted expansion.

In Kenya, African Cotton Industries Limited has produced cotton wool and hygiene supplies since 1960, operating facilities in Nairobi, Mombasa and Kampala.

The firm supplies major institutional distributors, including Mission for Essential Drugs and Supplies, the Kenya Medical Supplies Authority, and Kenyatta National Hospital.

In South Africa, Da Gama Textile now operates facilities with more than 580 employees, producing up to 15 million machine metres of fabric per month in Zwelitsha, Eastern Cape.

Its healthcare range now includes 100% cotton and poly cotton sheeting, linen, drapes, curtains, and uniforms with antimicrobial and water repellent finishes.

“Cotton-rich sheeting is in high demand from both public and private hospitals, as well as clinics and healthcare facilities to ensure patient comfort and laundering durability,” it noted.

The company says its medical fabrics are produced locally using mostly local materials and that its facilities have the capacity and equipment to make fabrics in different weights, designs and finishes.

South Africa has also moved further into specialised medical fabrics, with producers such as PrionTex entering this space. The company manufactures reusable laminates, theatre textiles, clean room suits, and procedure packs for African markets.

PrionTex also developed a breathable three-layer surgical gown fabric tested to EN 13795 standards to block fluids, viruses, and bacteria.

Zimbabwe, meanwhile, has developed another niche. Zimbabwe Hosiery now manufactures tubular medical bandages in two ranges. Its Tubidress range is made from 100% cotton yarn while its Perlon range uses cotton and polyester yarns.

“The Tubidress range of tubular medical bandages is manufactured from 100% cotton yarn,” the company said.

Such products may appear simple compared with high technology medical equipment, but they are part of the everyday supplies that hospitals need continuously.

That makes healthcare an attractive market for textile manufacturers in Africa’s cotton value chain. The demand is also being supported by a broader push to build local health production capacity.

In Morocco, the focus is already on medical goods. Chinese manufacturer Jiangsu Aishelun Medical Technology Group launched its first African factory at Mohammed VI Tanger Tech City in May 2026 through its Moroccan subsidiary, InnovMed Tech Group.

The company makes medical consumables and infection control items, from surgical gowns and drapes to ice packs, adult care products and urinary bags.

It plans to use the plant to serve markets across Europe, the Middle East and North Africa while sourcing raw materials across Africa.

Still, the World Health Organisation expects African countries to remain heavily dependent on imported medicines and health products and urges long-term manufacturing plans for countries.

Close 

Kenya’s 2026–2030 local health manufacturing plan, unveiled in June, recognises that production capacity alone will not build an industry. It calls for better use of existing factories and sustained procurement commitments that give manufacturers the certainty to invest and expand.

President William Ruto, who chairs the African Union’s push for local manufacturing, has placed the issue at the centre of what he calls Africa’s “health security and sovereignty agenda”. Kenya’s Principal Secretary for Medical Services, Dr Ouma Oluga, put the challenge more directly: “You cannot finance a healthcare system that you cannot supply.”

From surgical cotton wool in Zambia to hospital fabrics in South Africa and tubular bandages in Zimbabwe, African manufacturers are demonstrating that more of the continent’s cotton can be turned into essential medical products at home.

The decisive next step is whether hospitals, governments and procurement agencies will provide the reliable orders needed to turn those individual production lines into a durable continental industry.

World.title: South Africa: Tinubu Takes Fight Against Xenophobic, Afrophobic Attacks By South Africa to AU
World.content:
A man is attacked with a sjambok at an anti-immigrant March and March protest in Jeppestown.

President Bola Tinubu on Sunday formally lodged a complaint against the recurring xenophobic and Afrophobic attacks against Africans and other nationals in South Africa to the African Union (AU), warning that the incidents undermine the continent's solidarity, unity and peaceful coexistence.

He specifically requested prompt collective action from the continent's leaders, including the placement of this matter on the agenda for the 40th Ordinary Session of the Assembly.

Tinubu made Nigeria's position known in a message delivered by Vice-President Kashim Shettima, at the 21st Extraordinary Session of the Assembly of the African Union (AU) in Luanda, Angola.



The president called on the AU to place the matter on the agenda of the 40th Ordinary Session of the Assembly scheduled for January 2027, while urging African leaders to reaffirm their commitment to the safety, protection and dignity of all African nationals.

He declared: "Nigeria wishes to express its concern over the recurring xenophobic and Afrophobic attacks against Africans and other nationals in South Africa.

"While recognising South Africa's sovereign right to enforce its immigration laws and acknowledging its contributions to the continent, Nigeria stresses that such attacks undermine African solidarity, unity and peaceful coexistence, and require urgent collective attention.

"It is on this note that Nigeria calls on this august Assembly to place the matter on the agenda of the upcoming 40th Ordinary Session of the AU Assembly, scheduled for January 2027, for consideration and appropriate action."

Tinubu called for stronger continental efforts to combat xenophobia and Afrophobia, stressing that dialogue, preventive diplomacy, and collective action remained essential to preserving African unity.

On the wider security situation across the continent, Nigeria backed the adoption of the Luanda Action Plan as a practical roadmap for strengthening conflict prevention, arguing that preventing conflicts was cheaper and more sustainable than managing them after they erupt.

"For Nigeria, conflict prevention remains more cost-effective and sustainable than conflict management," the president said.

Tinubu warned that fragmented peace initiatives and increasing external interference through foreign military forces, mercenaries, and private defence contractors risk weakening the AU's conflict prevention mechanisms and the principle of African ownership.

He further called on arms-producing and exporting countries to strengthen cooperation with African states and prevent weapons and ammunition produced within their jurisdictions from being diverted to terrorists and other non-state armed groups.

The president maintained that while the AU has robust mechanisms for preventing and resolving conflicts, limited trust and inconsistent implementation continue to undermine their effectiveness.

Close 

"The growing reliance on external actors risks weakening African institutions and the principle of African ownership," he said, calling on member states to renew their commitment to collective responsibility for Africa's peace and security.

Nigeria also backed sustainable and predictable financing for AU peace operations and the full operationalisation of UN Security Council Resolution 2719 to strengthen the continental body's capacity to respond effectively to conflicts and crises.

Tinubu urged African leaders to recommit themselves to home-grown solutions, stronger cooperation, and shared responsibility in tackling the continent's security challenges.

"Let us therefore renew our collective commitment to solidarity, cooperation, and shared responsibility as we build the Africa we want," the president stated.

World.title: Niger: Attempted Coup - Niger Junta Still in Control, but Situation Remains Tense
World.content:
The situation in Niger Republic remains fluid after a mutiny was thwarted by national security forces in collaboration with Russian-linked Africa Corps

On Saturday, Niger Republic came under an attack by mutineers who attempted to seize power from the junta led by Abdourahamane Tchiani. After fighting that lasted for hours, Mr Tchiani's government still remains in power.

The mutinous soldiers took the regime by surprise, besieging and holding sway over the Diori Hamani International Airport and Air Base 101. They also attempted to breach the fortified perimeter of the presidential palace. The attack briefly disrupted the state television and radio broadcasts.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Footage seen by our reporter showed armed soldiers, tactical armoured vehicles and troops securing the streets of Niamey. The mutineers seized control of Air Base 101, the paratroopers' camp and other positions near the international airport.

The mutineers released a statement from the air base, announcing that Mr Tchiani was no longer the head of state. The statement, signed under the name of Armed Forces for the Restoration of the Fatherland, also announced the dissolution of the constitution, border closure and restriction of movement.

While the fighting continued, it was reported that the head of the junta requested the intervention of Africa Corps, a Russian-backed mercenary group which has entrenched itself in Sahelian states led by military rulers.

Before that, the mercenaries, stationed at the air base, had come under attack by the rebellious soldiers, prompting them to defend themselves. After a formal request to neutralise the mutineers, the Africa Corps collaborated with the Nigerien Presidential Guard, launching an air and ground offensive, making it a second primary mission in the region since their show of strength in Bamako in April.

This led to the killing and arrest of the mutinous soldiers, with the Nigerien government announcing that it remained in control.

In solidarity with Niger

In the face of the attempted mutiny, several countries sided with the junta in Niger.

Given its friction with the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS), it is expected that no member of the regional bloc will stand in solidarity with Niger. But its allies, Burkina Faso and Mali, with whom it co-founded the Alliance of Sahel States (AES), did throw their weight behind their falling member.

The AES, in a statement issued in Ouagadougou, affirmed it remained "fully committed to and mobilised alongside Niger, sharing its determination to continue the struggle for sovereignty and peace."

It also praised "the loyalty, courage, and sense of duty of the Nigerien Defence and Security Forces who, true to their oath, confronted this mutiny and helped restore order."

Affirming its solidarity with Niger and its people, the Turkiye Republic called for "restraint" to preserve the country's security and stability.

Algeria also assured the Niamey government of its "full solidarity and firm support" to help the nation overcome the ordeal and restore security.

Who are the mutineers?

The full identities of the mutinous soldiers remain sketchy at press time. However, footage of captured soldiers suggests that they are mainly young and junior-ranked personnel.

Yet, some unverified reports have linked some senior officers to the plot. Among them are Kimba Tahirou, a colonel, and Abdoulaye Idé, a captain promoted to the rank in 2021, according to I-Sahel.

According to social media claims, Mr Tahirou, who is the head of the national gendarmerie, has sided with the mutineers.

The government has not issued a statement to debunk these claims, and it has also not mentioned the names and ranks of the young officer arrested in connection with the incident.

Why the action?

Most of the soldiers that took part in the mutiny were drawn from active frontlines around Ouallam, Téra, and Dosso, including Tillabériwhere, suggesting that the action might have been triggered by worsening insecurity.

According to a jihadi researcher, Hasret Kargin, the mutiny erupted a day after the Nigerien junta released four al-Qaeda linked jihadists in exchange for 11 soldiers, a kind of policy that Mr Tchiani frowned at when he seized power in 2023.

The ousted President Mohamed Bazoum had pioneered the approach of dialogue, reconciliation and conditional amnesty as part of its counterterrorism strategies. But Mr Tchiani, upon overthrowing him, vowed a military-only approach.

A window for jihadists

Because soldiers abandoned their posts to stage the mutiny, jihadi groups like the Islamic State Sahel Province (ISSP), JNIM and other terror networks might take advantage of their absence and the ongoing instability to further entrench themselves in the country.

Close 

"The security vacuum in these regions will allow these armed groups to secure further gains in territories where they are already strong," Mr Kargin warned in an X post.

He urged the Nigerien government not to see the plot as a mere mutinous uprising, as "recurrence of similar crises would not be surprising."

Niger has suffered three similar attacks this year, with the two incidents staged by jihadists.

As of the time of this report, Niger's larger and more powerful neighbour, Nigeria, has yet to comment on the coup. The relationship between the two countries became tense when Mr Bazoum was ousted by Mr Tchiani's government.

Nigeria's President Bola Tinubu, who was the ECOWAS leader at the time, condemned the coup and led the regional organisation to impose sanctions and a blockade on Niger.

Although the blockade and sanctions have been lifted, the neighbours are yet to fully mend their relationship.

World.title: Rwanda: Over 7,000 to Retake National Exams After Mass Cheating
World.content:
A total of 7,188 primary school learners will retake the 2025/26 Primary Leaving Examinations after investigations confirmed mass cheating.

The Ministry of Education announced the decision on Sunday, August 30, saying the investigations found that cheating took place in 254 examination rooms across the country.

"Some of the malpractice was organised and facilitated by adults entrusted with administering the examinations," it said in a statement.

ALSO READ: National exams: Over 7,000 candidates under investigation over cheating



The affected learners had initially faced the possibility of having their examinations cancelled, which is the normal consequence of examination malpractice.

However, the Ministry said the circumstances of the case warranted giving the learners another opportunity to sit the examinations.

"In the interest of fairness and the future of the affected learners, the Ministry has therefore decided to allow them to retake the Primary Leaving Examinations," the Ministry said.

The examinations will be administered from September 2 to 4, 2026.

The National Examination and School Inspection Authority (NESA) is expected to release the exams timetable, designated examination centres and further guidance on Monday.

ALSO READ: Key takeaways from 2025/26 PLE, O-Level national exams

The Minister of Education, Joseph Nsengimana, had said on Friday that the 7,000 was the highest number of cases of malpractices ever reported in national exams.

The examination results of the candidates suspected of cheating had been withheld as investigators were looking into the matter.

The Ministry said it will work closely with NESA, learners, parents, schools and local authorities to ensure the retake process is conducted with minimal disruption.

The Ministry further said individuals found to have organised, facilitated, participated in or deliberately enabled the malpractice would be held accountable.

The affected students are part of 286,579 students who sat Primary Leaving Examinations from 3,895 schools.

NESA reported that 82.2 per cent of candidates passed the examinations.

World.title: Rwanda: No Backing Down in Fight Against Illicit Alcohol, Says Youth Minister
World.content:
Some illicit beverages seized in Gatsibo on Tuesday, August 4. Rwanda FDA on Tuesday, August 4, announced the closure of 27 companies, as part of the ongoing crackdown on illicit alcohol production and distribution.

The Minister of Youth and Arts, Dr Abdallah Utumatwishima, urged young people to protect their lives by avoiding the use of illicit alcohol brands that have been recalled.

Utumatwishima also warned anyone holding onto stock of recalled alcohol brands, hoping to sell them clandestinely or when the ongoing crackdown eases, saying the campaign is only beginning.

ALSO READ: Govt renews efforts to tackle alcohol abuse among youth

The minister said this on Saturday, August 29, as he joined residents of the City of Kigali for Umuganda activities in Kicukiro Districr, which featured discussions on the fight against illicit alcohol and drug abuse.



"We must understand that good health is the capital for getting employment," he said.

The minister said part of his responsibility is to work with other institutions to create jobs for young people. However, he said some miss such opportunities because of health problems linked to alcohol and drug abuse.

ALSO READ: Govt taps artistes in campaign against alcohol, drug abuse

Utumatwishima also urged young people to continue their education and improve their skills to meet labour market demands.

He called on citizens to work with authorities to locate illicit alcohol production sites and those involved in the illegal activities.

The minister urged people to share information about where illicit alcohol is still being kept and called on those holding such products to come forward. He also called for a system that would allow people to provide information anonymously.

ALSO READ: Experts explain how illicit alcohol causes blindness, organ damage

Inspector General of Police CG Félix Namuhoranye used the Umuganda to highlight the risks of alcohol and drug abuse among young people, citing a recent incident in Kicukiro.

He said police recently found more than 50 young people, including minors, intoxicated and using different substances at a house party.

He said some of them were taken to hospital after fainting due to alcohol.

"Some of them had never tasted alcohol before and started drinking that day. Others were already drunk, while others were smoking marijuana," he said.

The police chief said the incident showed that the problem among young people extends beyond alcohol, with some having access to substances including marijuana, heroin and cocaine.

He warned against excessive drinking, saying alcohol can have serious consequences for those who consume it.

"However much you drink, you cannot finish alcohol; alcohol can finish you," he said.

Close 

ALSO READ: The fight against illicit alcohol is not over - Minister Habimana

Namuhoranye also challenged parents and guardians to take greater responsibility for knowing what keeps their children busy, especially at night.

He said some parents were asleep while their underage children were at the party and only learned about it after police called them.

"If you have a 15-year-old sister, do not go to bed without knowing where she spent the night. Do not sleep without knowing what she is doing wherever she has gone," he said.

He urged people who do not use drugs to help those struggling with substance abuse and become "agents of change" in their communities.

Umuganda also included awareness activities, with musician Riderman performing for residents at Gahanga Cricket Stadium after the community work and discussions on the dangers of illicit alcohol and the role of citizens in tackling the problem.

The renewed focus comes as authorities intensify the crackdown on illicit alcoholic beverages.

Since early August, officials said more than Rwf2.6 billion worth of illicit alcoholic beverages had been seized, while nearly 250 production sites involved in making the drinks had been shut down.

World.title: Accused NC killer mom plans insanity defense — as retired judge says more may follow Lindsay Clancy strategy
World.content:

The insanity defense planned by a North Carolina mother accused of killing her son has drawn parallels to Lindsay Clancy’s trial and raised questions about whether it could become prevalent in criminal cases.

Andrea Faust, 41, is charged with murder and attempted murder in the Feb. 12 death of her 3-year-old son and the attempted murder of her 2-year-old son at their home in Durham, North Carolina.

Her attorneys have filed notice that they intend to rely on defenses of not guilty by reason of insanity and diminished capacity, WRAL reported.

The case is drawing parallels to Clancy’s Massachusetts trial. Retired Massachusetts Superior Judge Jack Lu said he expects similar defenses to be raised more often as the Clancy case draws national attention to postpartum mental-health conditions.

LINDSAY CLANCY DIDN'T SHOW 'BREAK WITH REALITY' AS JURY WEIGHS PSYCHOSIS DEFENSE: SUSAN SMITH PROSECUTOR

Clancy has pleaded not guilty by reason of lack of criminal responsibility in the 2023 deaths of her three children. Her defense argued she suffered from postpartum psychosis, while prosecutors argue she understood her actions and acted deliberately.

Jurors ended a second day of deliberations Friday without reaching a verdict. They will return on Monday morning to continue working toward a verdict.

In Faust’s case, the filing does not establish that she was legally insane or had diminished capacity. Her attorney, Nicole Galinsky, told the local outlet that a defense expert concluded Faust could not distinguish right from wrong during the alleged murders.

"Andrea and Lindsay’s cases are eerily similar, though not entirely the same," Galinsky told Fox News Digital.

Galinsky noted that Faust was not suffering from postpartum psychosis.

"However, both women were known to be loving, doting, responsible mothers who were worried about and caring for their children up until the very second they decided to kill them," Galinsky said, adding that Faust and Clancy were both struggling with similar issues, including hallucinations, hospitalizations and mental health.

"Neither woman did this out of the blue," Galinsky said in an email. "Both were struggling enormously with their mental health. But, like most women and almost all moms, they were just trying to get through each day, care for their children, be a good mom/wife/employee. Both were seeking help from doctors who weren’t really taking their concerns seriously.

"Both of these cases highlight the failure in our society to take women and mothers seriously when it comes to their mental health. Both of these women advocated for themselves countless times and—for what? It got them nowhere.

"I am hopeful that our case will demonstrate how to properly treat and rehabilitate a woman living her own worst nightmare. Lindsay Clancy was not given that luxury."

FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X

Lu said society and the legal system have not fully understood the effects postpartum mental illness can have on behavior and criminal responsibility.

"Most of the time, these criminal responsibility, insanity, mental health defenses are unsuccessful," Lu told Fox News Digital.

LINDSAY CLANCY'S FAMILY WAS 'VERY CONCERNED' ABOUT HER MENTAL HEALTH IN THE MONTHS BEFORE SHE KILLED HER KIDS

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS

Although he is not a mental-health expert, Lu said the Clancy trial has challenged and changed his own understanding of what a person might experience.

"I had no real understanding of what a person like Ms. Clancy was going through until this trial," he said.

SEND US A TIP

Faust was found incapable of proceeding to trial in March after court records documented serious concerns about her mental health and safety, according to WRAL.

GOT A TIP?

Central Regional Hospital later found her capable of proceeding as of May 21. Her attorney said another evaluation would examine her mental state at the time of the alleged offenses.

GET BREAKING NEWS BY EMAIL

Lu said mental-health defenses should receive more serious consideration because they can explain behavior and reduce moral culpability. But allegations involving children create an especially difficult path with jurors, he said.
